item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Nasdaq et S&P 500 en hausse avec le rebond des valeurs liées à l'IA
item.description: Le Nasdaq et le S&P 500 ont rebondi lundi à Wall Street portés par le rebond des valeurs liées à l'intelligence artificielle après le fort mouvement de vente de la semaine dernière, tandis que le recul des cours du pétrole a également soutenu la tendance avant une série de résultats d'entreprises très attendus.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le Nasdaq et le S&P 500 ont rebondi lundi à Wall Street portés par le rebond des valeurs liées à l'intelligence artificielle après le fort mouvement de vente de la semaine dernière, tandis que le recul des cours du pétrole a également soutenu la tendance avant une série de résultats d'entreprises très attendus. L'indice Dow Jones (.DJI) a cédé 0,07%, ou 36,38 points, à 51.966,03 points. Le Standard & Poor's 500 (.SPX) , plus large, a pris 31,29 points, soit 0,41% à 7.690,73 points. Le Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) a avancé de son côté de 290,85 points, soit 1,11% à 26.430,886 points. Le S&P 500 et le Nasdaq avaient enregistré vendredi leur plus forte baisse hebdomadaire depuis fin juin, les inquiétudes selon lesquelles des taux d'intérêt plus élevés pourraient freiner les investissements dans les infrastructures d'intelligence artificielle ayant pesé sur les valeurs technologiques, en particulier les opérateurs de centres de données. Ce mouvement de repli traduisait les interrogations croissantes des investisseurs sur le financement des dépenses massives liées au développement de l'intelligence artificielle, une question qui exerce une pression grandissante sur les entreprises ayant soutenu le marché haussier américain, récemment entré dans sa quatrième année. Les fabricants de semi-conducteurs ont également participé au rebond de lundi. Broadcom (AVGO.O) a avancé de 1,77% et Micron Technology (MU.O) a bondi de 2,96%. item.title: Bericht: Nscale verhandelt mit Anthropic über 45-Milliarden-Dollar-Deal

Dabei gehe es um eine zweite Anlage auf dem sogenannten Monarch-Campus im Bundesstaat West Virginia. item.content:encoded: Der von Nvidia (NVDA.O) unterstützte Rechenzentrumsbetreiber Nscale steht einem Medienbericht zufolge vor einem weiteren milliardenschweren Geschäft mit dem KI-Entwickler Anthropic. Nscale verhandle mit dem Anbieter des Chatbots Claude über den Verkauf von Rechenleistung im Wert von rund 45 Milliarden Dollar, meldete die Nachrichtenagentur Bloomberg am Montag unter Berufung auf Insider. Dabei gehe es um eine zweite Anlage auf dem sogenannten Monarch-Campus im Bundesstaat West Virginia. Diese solle eine Kapazität von 460 Megawatt liefern und mit den modernen Vera-Rubin-KI-Chips von Nvidia ausgestattet werden. Nscale und Anthropic äußerten sich zunächst nicht zu dem Bericht. Anthropic hatte im August einen ähnlichen Vertrag über 45 Milliarden Dollar für die erste Anlage auf dem Campus abgeschlossen. Dem Bericht zufolge hat sich das KI-Unternehmen zudem ein Vorkaufsrecht für ein geplantes drittes Gebäude gesichert. Nscale musste zuletzt einen Rückschlag hinnehmen: Microsoft (MSFT.O) hatte sich aus einem Projekt für ein Vorzeige-Rechenzentrum zurückgezogen, da sich der Stromanschluss verzögerte und die Inbetriebnahme auf die 2030er Jahre verschoben wurde. Gleichzeitig wächst an den Finanzmärkten die Skepsis gegenüber der schuldenfinanzierten Expansion der KI-Infrastruktur. In der vergangenen Woche war die Aktie des Nscale-Rivalen CoreWeave (CRWV.O) wegen Sorgen über dessen Schuldenberg von 50 Milliarden Dollar eingebrochen. Nscale ist seit seiner Gründung stark gewachsen und hat sein Vertragsvolumen innerhalb von zweieinhalb Jahren von 100 Millionen auf mehr als 103 Milliarden Dollar gesteigert.

item.title: Trump juge que Kyiv devrait écarter Zelensky des négociations
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré lundi qu'il estimait qu'une autre personne que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky devrait négocier au nom de Kyiv dans le cadre des efforts visant à mettre fin à la guerre avec la Russie.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré lundi qu'il estimait qu'une autre personne que le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky devrait négocier au nom de Kyiv dans le cadre des efforts visant à mettre fin à la guerre avec la Russie. "Il est peut-être temps que Zelensky fasse appel à quelqu'un d'autre pour négocier", a déclaré Donald Trump, qui avait appelé le 10 octobre à remplacer le président ukrainien. Donald Trump a également déclaré à des journalistes que la Russie avait été "correcte" concernant l'Ukraine. "Ils n'ont pas fait grand-chose", a-t-il dit. Donald Trump a ajouté que les États-Unis continuaient à partager des renseignements avec l'Ukraine et qu'il envisagerait d'autoriser les Ukrainiens à rester aux États-Unis sous le régime du statut de protection temporaire jusqu'à la fin de la guerre.

item.title: France-Vinted retire de la vente les articles soupçonnés d'être volés en marge des manifestations
item.description: L'application dédiée à l'achat et à la vente de vêtements d'occasion Vinted a annoncé lundi avoir renforcé les contrôles sur les annonces suspectes et supprimé celles revendant des biens pillés en marge des manifestations de ce weekend en France.
item.dc:creator: Anna Peverieri
item.content:encoded: L'application dédiée à l'achat et à la vente de vêtements d'occasion Vinted a annoncé lundi avoir renforcé les contrôles sur les annonces suspectes et supprimé celles revendant des biens pillés en marge des manifestations de ce weekend en France. De nombreuses scènes de violence et de pillages ont terni samedi la journée de mobilisation contre la vie chère qui a rassemblé des centaines de milliers de personnes dans toute la France. Vinted a précisé que ses équipes avaient pris des "mesures immédiates" dès ce week-end pour identifier et supprimer les annonces soupçonnées d’être liées aux pillages, ajoutant que la surveillance des annonces suspectes avait été renforcée. Les comptes reconnus coupables d'avoir enfreint ses règles pourraient faire l'objet d'une exclusion définitive, a précisé l'entreprise. "La vente de biens volés, ou le fait d'en faire la promotion, est strictement interdite sur Vinted, et nous appliquons une tolérance zéro à cet égard", a déclaré un porte-parole dans un communiqué. L'entreprise a dit qu'elle collaborait avec les forces de l'ordre et les autorités françaises et qu'elle continuerait à adapter ses processus pour identifier et contrer les risques émergents et les comportements malveillants. La France constitue l'un des principaux marchés de Vinted, société créée en 2008 par un couple à Vilnius, capitale de la Lituanie. La place de marché en ligne interdit la vente d’articles volés et s'appuie, entre autres contrôles, sur les signalements des commerçants et des utilisateurs pour détecter les annonces suspectes.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan und Südkorea haben einer Studie zufolge bei der Anwendung von Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) aufgeholt und sind in die Weltspitze vorgerückt. Deutschland tritt dagegen auf der Stelle und ist nicht in der Weltspitze, wie die Beratungsgesellschaft Boston Consulting Group (BCG) am Dienstag in Düsseldorf mitteilte. Deutschland habe aber großes Potenzial, vor allem mit KI in der Industrie. Allerdings fehlten Fachkräfte in dem Bereich. Japan punktet laut BCG mit einer innovationsfreundlichen Regulierung, umfangreichen Investitionen internationaler Technologiekonzerne und einer starken Robotik-Industrie. Südkorea habe gezielt in eigene KI-Modelle und Rechenkapazitäten investiert. Beide Staaten hätten seit 2024 die Voraussetzungen für den Einsatz von KI deutlich verbessert. "Es reicht nicht aus, KI auf politischer Ebene zur Priorität zu erklären", sagte BCG-Experte Andrej Levin. "Entscheidend ist, wie schnell daraus Investitionen, Infrastruktur und konkrete Anwendungen entstehen." Insgesamt haben sich seit 2024 acht Länder so deutlich verbessert, dass sie in eine höhere Klasse vorgerückt sind. In der Weltspitze sind neben den Aufsteigern Japan und Südkorea weiterhin die USA, China, Großbritannien, Kanada und Singapur. Deutschland bleibt gleich und gehört nicht zu den weltweit führenden KI-Standorten. BCG hat für die Studie insgesamt 79 Staaten unter die Lupe genommen. INDUSTRIE AM ZUG Die Entwicklung besonders leistungsfähiger KI-Modelle ist laut Studie weiterhin stark auf die USA und China konzentriert. "Deutschland muss nicht jedes KI-Modell selbst entwickeln, um wirtschaftlich erfolgreich zu sein", so Levin. "Die große Chance liegt darin, Künstliche Intelligenz dort einzusetzen, wo wir bereits über industrielle Kompetenz und jahrzehntelanges Prozesswissen verfügen." Gute Voraussetzungen dafür gebe es in den Industriezweigen Automobil, Chemie, Biotechnologie und Medizintechnik. "Mit der Weiterentwicklung sogenannter Physical AI, also KI-Systemen zur Steuerung von Maschinen, Robotern und Fahrzeugen, könnten künftig auch industrielle Bereiche wie Produktion und Logistik stärker von KI-bedingten Veränderungen erfasst werden." Rund 65 Prozent der deutschen Wirtschaftsleistung entfallen laut BCG-Analyse auf Branchen mit mittlerem oder hohem KI-Veränderungspotenzial. Nötig seien nun qualifizierte Fachkräfte, Investitionen und der Zugang zu leistungsfähiger Recheninfrastruktur. "Insbesondere bei der Verfügbarkeit spezialisierter KI-Fachkräfte besteht hierzulande gegenüber den führenden Volkswirtschaften Nachholbedarf", warnte BCG. "In Sachen Risikokapital und Finanzierung von KI-Unternehmen weist Deutschland jedoch im internationalen Vergleich Stärken auf." Die Bundesregierung will bis 2030 die deutschen Rechenzentrumskapazitäten verdoppeln und die Rechenkapazitäten für KI und Supercomputer vervierfachen.

item.title: Foreign banks’ India strategy: Buy, don’t build
item.description: Foreign lenders are rediscovering Indian banking, but now they're buying their way in rather than building from scratch.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal
item.content:encoded: Foreign lenders are rediscovering Indian banking, but now they're buying their way in rather than building from scratch. Will these deep-pocketed investors shake up the industry? That's our focus this week. Write to me with your views at ira.dugal@thomsonreuters.com . And, youth protests continue in India's national capital of New Delhi. Scroll down for all the developments and an analysis on what's pushing young people to take to the streets. THIS WEEK IN ASIA [USN:L6N45Y0AP TEXT:"This Chinese export boom really has legs – and wings"] [USN:L1N4650UG TEXT:"Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month"] [USN:L1N4620AO TEXT:"Indonesia faces rare MSCI exclusion that could cut it off from global capital"] [USN:L6N45U0Y7 TEXT:"Iran ships some LPG, jet fuel despite US blockade, data shows"] [USN:L1N46500R TEXT:"Beijing's population expected to become super-aged by 2035"] WHY BUILD WHEN YOU CAN BUY? After years on the fringes of Indian banking, foreign lenders are spending billions to buy the scale they've found difficult to build organically. Canada’s Fairfax Financial Holdings last week clinched a [USN:L1N4600FH TEXT:"$5.56 billion deal"] for a majority stake in IDBI Bank from its two largest shareholders, the Indian government and state-owned insurer Life Insurance Corporation. Fairfax founder Prem Watsa, on an investor call, called it a “once-in-a-lifetime opportunity” to gain control of a bank in one of the world’s fastest-growing economies. The Canadian investor [USN:L4N46111L TEXT:"plans to fold"] other Indian financial investments into IDBI, creating a business that spans lending, insurance and capital markets. Fairfax is not alone. Rare for years, deals for control of Indian banks have suddenly picked up as mid-sized lenders look overseas for the deep-pocketed investors needed to fund their next phase of growth. Last year, Japan’s Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation bought a [USN:L2N3V40AF TEXT:"24% stake"] in Yes Bank from a group of investors that had rescued the lender in 2020, while Dubai’s Emirates NBD agreed to [USN:L1N3VZ02G TEXT:"buy a 60% stake"] in RBL Bank for $3 billion. Other recent deals include Bank of America agreeing to buy a [USN:L4N4491G9 TEXT:"49.9% stake"] in Mukesh Ambani-backed non-bank lender Jio Financial Services for $1.9 billion, giving it access to a retail and small business banking franchise. “These deals suggest that investors favoured financial services platforms with scale, regulatory oversight, and substantial capital requirements,” Grant Thornton said in a note. Mergers and acquisitions in India’s financial sector hit $4.1 billion between January and September, according to Grant Thornton, even before the IDBI transaction was announced. [USN:L4N46019R TEXT:"Read here"] for more on some of the biggest deals. FROM RETREAT TO RETURN Foreign banks have had a patchy record in India. American and European lenders expanded aggressively in India in the early 2000s, only to pull back as the global financial crisis, tougher international capital rules and a punishing domestic bad-loan cycle took their toll. This latest wave of investments is different. The money is coming from a broader set of geographies, notably Japan, the Middle East and North America. And instead of building branch networks and customer bases from scratch, investors are buying into established franchises. Indian banks' improved operational metrics and reasonable valuations make them an attractive bet, analysts say. “Bad debts are at multi-decade lows, credit demand remains healthy, and a supportive liquidity backdrop coupled with recent rate hikes will support net interest margins going forward,” said Dan Billis, associate portfolio manager at UK-based investment management firm Alquity. Valuations remain close to the trough, with the sector trading two standard deviations below its 10-year historical average, Billis said. The regulator has also opened the door wider. On paper, regulations place a 15% limit on a single foreign financial institution's shareholding in an Indian bank. But the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has allowed foreign lenders to take majority or controlling stakes in some Indian banks, granting case-by-case exceptions. So what happens when billions of dollars of foreign capital meets an already fiercely competitive banking market? One early battleground could be talent. Indian banking has already [USN:L4N44S0PE TEXT:"seen reshuffling"] at the top and as new investors overhaul businesses and pursue growth, employee churn could remain elevated, Jefferies said in a note last week. The bigger question is whether the new owners can succeed where foreign banks have struggled before in India: turning deep pockets into meaningful market share. MARKET MATTERS The Indian market is considered generally bereft of AI investment opportunities — one reason the benchmark equity indices have underperformed global peers. But a handful of stocks considered proxies have rallied sharply this year. [USN:L4N45V07Q TEXT:"Read this report"] by my colleague Vivek Kumar M. YOUTH PROTESTS Protests against India's top election commission official continue in New Delhi, with a leader of the "cockroach" youth movement [USN:L1N46300N TEXT:"arrested"] and later released. Protesters want election chief Gyanesh Kumar to resign after a review of the electoral rolls led to millions of voters being removed. [USN:L4N45Z0IJ TEXT:"Read here to understand more"]. There are likely to be more street protests in India this year than at any time in the past decade, the independent conflict monitor Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) has said. What's fuelling the discontent? [USN:L6N46206J TEXT:"Read this analysis"] by Reuters' colleagues Tora Agarwala, Saurabh Sharma and Sunil Kataria.

item.title: ALCS notebook: Freddy Peralta nabs MVP honors after second win
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Two days after pitching (briefly) out of the bullpen, Tampa Bay Rays starter Freddy Peralta delivered another effective outing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- Two days after pitching (briefly) out of the bullpen, Tampa Bay Rays starter Freddy Peralta delivered another effective outing. His work in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday wasn't as flashy as his Game 2 masterpiece, but it was effective enough for Peralta to seal the Most Valuable Player award as the Rays advanced to the World Series with a 7-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians. Peralta tossed 5 1/3 innings on Monday, allowing one run on five hits with three walks and three strikeouts. He earned his second victory of the series, having fired six shutout innings to help Tampa Bay level the ALCS in Game 2 and then getting two outs for a hold in Game 4. "This is for the boys!" Peralta shouted after being presented the MVP trophy. Peralta flourished after a deadline trade brought him from a struggling situation with the New York Mets to Tampa Bay for three prospects. The 30-year-old veteran went 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA in 10 starts with Tampa Bay to finish the regular season and was selected the AL Pitcher of the Month for September after going 4-0 with a 0.96 ERA over five starts and 28 innings. Through four postseason appearances (three starts) this month, Peralta is 2-0 with a 1.08 ERA. Peralta's renaissance is the result of a potent combination of a new glute-heavy workout regimen, pitching out of the stretch full time at the encouragement of the coaching staff and discovering a home-field advantage he couldn't have better customized for himself. Located at close to sea level, Tropicana Field features a windless, 72-degree environment that has made it one of the most pitcher-friendly parks in the major leagues. "Fastball Freddy" possesses a calling-card four-seam fastball that has a tendency to stay flat deep into its path in home games, staying high in or just out of the strike zone, with extra velocity keeping it away from the barrels of wide-eyed hitters. "You cannot fight with him up in the zone," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. FLAT, OUT: The performance of Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was emblematic of the stifling effort by Rays pitchers. The hero of a comeback from two-games-to-none down against the Chicago White Sox in the AL Division Series, Ramirez went 5-for-8 with two runs and an RBI in Games 1 and 3 wins against the Rays but 1-for-11 with no runs nor RBIs thereafter as Tampa Bay took the final three contests. Rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter was similarly smothered before going 2-for-5 with two runs on Monday. And despite hitting a game-sealing two-run double in Game 1, Jo Adell finished 3-for-22 (.136) with just those two RBIs in the series. When asked his advice for his players after falling short, Vogt said, "Let it hurt. Let it sink in." ARMS RACE: Cleveland used seven pitchers to account for eight innings on Monday. They allowed seven runs, seven hits and six walks while striking out just three. Opener Shawn Armstrong, who pitched 1 1/3 innings out of the bullpen in Game 5 on Sunday, was charged with one run in Game 6, exiting after allowing a leadoff single to cleanup hitter Junior Caminero in the second. He threw nine pitches. Replacement Tim Herrin nearly escaped what became a two-run Rays rally after a fielder's choice and a walk to Victor Mesa Jr., but after a contorting check swing with two outs, Richie Palacios banged a two-run line-drive double to right-center. Matt Festa ultimately escaped a bases-loaded jam in the inning. Vogt said after his team's Game 5 loss that workhorse starter Gavin Williams, who pitched in relief in the ALDS, was not available after starting and pitching five innings for the Guardians' ALCS Game 3 win on Thursday. He noted that starter Tanner Bibee wasn't used in the series at all because an opportunity never arose. Cade Smith, who tied the Rays' Bryan Baker for the American League lead in saves (41) in the regular season, worked the seventh, allowing a two-run homer to Caminero. --Brant James, Field Level Media

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Der Elektrotechnikkonzern ABB (ABBN.S) beschleunigt das Wachstumstempo weiter. Getrieben vom Boom beim Bau von Rechenzentren kletterte der Auftragseingang im dritten Quartal um 40 Prozent auf 12,06 Milliarden Dollar, wie das Schweizer Unternehmen am Dienstag mitteilte. Im zweiten Quartal hatte ABB ein Bestellungsplus von bereinigt 28 Prozent verbucht, im ersten Quartal von 24 Prozent. In der größten und profitabelsten Sparte Elektrifizierung schoss der Auftragseingang im Sommer gar um 70 Prozent hoch. Zudem gründe ABB ein Gemeinschaftsunternehmen mit Mitsubishi Electric (6503.T) , in das dessen ausgegliedertes Produktgeschäft für Niederspannungs-Energieverteilung eingebracht werde. Das Joint Venture werde sich auf Niederspannungsprodukte für Märkte in Asien konzentrieren. Für umgerechnet rund 495 Millionen Dollar werde ABB eine Mehrheitsbeteiligung von 51 Prozent an dem neu formierten Unternehmen erwerben und zudem die damit verbundenen Vertriebsaktivitäten von Mitsubishi Electric für Niederspannungs-Energieverteilungsprodukte außerhalb Japans komplett übernehmen. Die Transaktion werde voraussichtlich in der zweiten Jahreshälfte 2027 abgeschlossen. ABB habe mittelfristig eine Option auf eine vollständige Übernahme der verbleibenden Anteile.

Premierminister Sebastien Lecornu hatte eine flächendeckende Ausgangssperre für die Hauptstadt ausgeschlossen, nicht jedoch die Ausrufung des Notstands. item.title: Chinese navy says US ship near Sabina Shoal jeopardised maritime security
item.description: China's Southern Theater Command Navy on Tuesday accused a US littoral combat ship of jeopardising maritime security by "illegally" entering waters near Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without approval from Beijing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's Southern Theater Command Navy on Tuesday accused a US littoral combat ship of jeopardising maritime security by "illegally" entering waters near Sabina Shoal in the Spratly Islands without approval from Beijing. The Chinese navy dispatched forces to track and monitor the USS Charleston, and said the US action not only infringes on China's sovereign rights but was also detrimental to regional peace and stability. China and the Philippines, which shares a mutual defence treaty with the US, both contest sovereignty over Sabina Shoal and the entire Spratly Islands archipelago. The US Navy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Die deutsche Wirtschaft hat nach Einschätzung von Jensen Huang gute Voraussetzungen für den erfolgreichen Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI). Die Unternehmen verfügten über ausgezeichnetes Fachwissen und einen wertvollen industriellen Datenschatz, sagte der Chef des weltgrößten Chipkonzerns Nvidia (NVDA.O) bei der Konferenz "Invest in Germany" am Montag. Dies sei eine starke Basis, um mithilfe von KI künftiges Wachstum anzukurbeln. Diese Gelegenheit dürfe Deutschland nicht verstreichen lassen. "Diese industrielle Revolution ist so gewaltig, dass man keine zweite Chance erhält." Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) äußerte sich bei der Podiumsdiskussion mit Huang ähnlich. Er appellierte an den deutschen Mittelstand: "Bitte öffnen Sie Ihre Türen für KI, damit diese Ihre Daten nutzen kann. Das ist für die Zukunft Deutschlands von entscheidender Bedeutung." Durch die Kombination bereits vorhandener Unternehmensdaten und neuer Technologien könne Deutschland zur führenden Nation im Bereich industrieller KI aufsteigen. Die Chancen hierfür stehen nach Einschätzung von Professor Björn Ommer, dem Leiter der Computer Vision & Learning Group an der Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, nicht schlecht. Anders als in anderen Technologiebereichen sei Europa bei sogenannter Physischer KI noch nicht abgeschlagen. Daher müsse hier gezielt investiert werden. BUND UND NVIDIA KOOPERIEREN BEI KI-ROBOTIK Aus diesem Grund schloss der Bund eine Partnerschaft mit Nvidia zur Weiterentwicklung KI-gesteuerter Roboter. Das Wirtschafts- und das Forschungsministerium unterzeichneten eine entsprechende Absichtserklärung mit dem US-Chipkonzern. Hierfür werde Nvidia seine Zusammenarbeit mit deutschen Partnern ausbauen, hieß es. Der Konzern mache seine KI-Modelle künftig neben der Großindustrie auch kleineren und mittleren Unternehmen sowie Forschungseinrichtungen zugänglich. Die Verschmelzung von klassischem Ingenieurwissen mit moderner Technologie solle die Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und technologische Souveränität Deutschlands sichern. Tamim Asfour, Professor für Humanoide Robotiksysteme am Karlsruher Institut für Technologie, begrüßte die Vereinbarung prinzipiell. Sie müsse aber an klare Bedingungen geknüpft werden. "Ob die Kooperation unsere Unabhängigkeit stärkt, entscheidet sich daran, wem die Daten, die trainierten Modelle und die Software-Werkzeuge gehören, die darauf entstehen, und ob sie offen und auf andere Hardware übertragbar bleiben." Zu möglichen Investitionen im Rahmen der Kooperation machte der Bund zunächst keine Angaben. Einem Medienbericht zufolge will er das Projekt mit einem [USN:L8N46210Z TEXT:"dreistelligen Millionenbetrag"] unterstützen. Das Geld solle unter anderem dazu dienen, Rechenkapazitäten in der [USN:L8N3Z01MT TEXT:"KI-Cloud"] der Deutschen Telekom (DTEGn.DE) anzumieten. MERZ: "DEUTSCHLAND IST OFFEN FÜR INVESTITIONEN" Bundeskanzler Merz warb bei der Veranstaltung darüber hinaus um Investitionen aus aller Welt. Er empfahl die Bundesrepublik als verlässlichen und stabilen Standort, der dem Multilateralismus, dem internationalen Handel und offenen Märkten verpflichtet sei. Huang verwies auf Nvidias Entwicklungsbüro in Berlin und die zahlreichen Beteiligungen an deutschen Unternehmen wie dem Roboterbauer Agile Robots. Zudem gab er den Einstieg bei Reflex Aerospace bekannt. Über die Höhe der Investitionssumme machte er keine Angaben. Der Berliner Satelliten-Hersteller teilte mit, das Geld diene dem Ausbau der Produktionskapazitäten .

item.title: OVHcloud meets 2026 targets, posts first positive cash flow since IPO
item.description: French cloud operator OVHcloud said on Tuesday its revenue rose 7.2% to €1.15 billion ($1.29 billion) in the year to August 31, and that it posted its first positive levered free cash flow since its 2021 listing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: French cloud operator OVHcloud (OVH.PA) said on Tuesday its revenue rose 7.2% to €1.15 billion ($1.29 billion) in the year to August 31, and that it posted its first positive levered free cash flow since its 2021 listing. The milestone means the French group now covers its heavy capital spending from its own operations, after five years of losses on cash generation since the listing. It also forecast growth above 10% for fiscal 2027, up from 7.2% this year. Levered free cash flow reached €24.7 million, against a negative €27.0 million a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA rose 9.7% to €480.5 million, a margin of 42.0%, while Public cloud revenue rose 18.9% to €255.1 million. CEO Octave Klaba said the year had been one of "discipline" and that the group had "returned to its fundamentals". For fiscal 2027, the company targets comparable growth above 10%, an adjusted EBITDA margin above 42.5% and positive levered free cash flow. ($1 = 0.8904 euros)

item.title: ABB says data centre business booming, Q3 figures in line with forecasts
item.description: ABB is continuing to see a boom in spending on data centres used to power artificial intelligence, the engineering group said on Tuesday, as it reported its latest earnings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ABB (ABBN.S) is continuing to see a boom in spending on data centres used to power artificial intelligence, the engineering group said on Tuesday, as it reported its latest earnings. The Swiss company said its operational earnings before interest, tax and amortisation jumped 24% to $2.03 billion in the three months to the end of September, slightly ahead of analyst forecasts for $2.0 billion. Revenue meanwhile rose 14% to $9.70 billion, slightly below forecasts of $9.74 billion in a company gathered consensus. ABB, which makes electrification and automation products used by factories, ships and ports, has been seeing strong demand for products like power distribution and cooling systems used in data centres. A surge in spending on AI and data centres is propping up the global economy, helping it withstand the energy shock from the Middle East war, the IMF said [USN:L1N45Z01U TEXT:"last week"], although it said a reassessment of efficiency gains from adopting the technology could dent investment. During the third quarter ABB said it had seen a triple digit increase in orders for data centre products, continuing the trend it saw during the second quarter.

item.title: Volkswagen bet on Xpeng to save its China business. It's not going to plan
item.description: When Volkswagen turned to EV maker Xpeng in 2023 to help fix its flailing Chinese business, executives touted the partnership as a shortcut to developing cars tailored for China at the high speed of the local auto sector.
item.dc:creator: Ju-min Park, Christina Amann
item.content:encoded: When Volkswagen turned to EV maker Xpeng in 2023 to help fix its flailing Chinese business, executives touted the partnership as a shortcut to developing cars tailored for China at the high speed of the local auto sector. Three years later, the alliance’s first product exemplifies Volkswagen’s descent in the world’s largest car market. The ID. UNYX 08 electric SUV sold an average of 267 vehicles a month between its April launch and August, data from automotive consultancy ThinkerCar show. That’s a fraction of the 3,622 monthly sales Volkswagen initially aimed to achieve this year, according to company planning documents. The weak debut reflects Volkswagen’s battle to revive its fortunes in China, where it reigned for decades until 2022 as the top automaker. China represents the challenge at the heart of Volkswagen’s global crisis: A market that once contributed nearly 50% of group profits now accounts for about 10%. That stunning reversal has forced the company into the [USN:L8N4570XW TEXT:"biggest restructuring"] in its 89-year history. The UNYX 08 also highlights a persistent problem in Volkswagen's China strategy. Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) recognized the market’s shift toward higher-end technology and sought local partners to catch up. Yet the German automaker struggled to turn those bets into commercial success. This report is based on a Reuters review of previously unreported company documents and interviews with six people familiar with Volkswagen, including current and former executives and consultants. It shows the automaker's ambitions ran ahead of what its products, pricing and sales strategy could deliver. Volkswagen sold the UNYX 08 through a nascent and limited distribution network. The vehicle also struggled against newer, software-laden Chinese electric SUVs. Spectators watch as Volkswagen ID. UNYX 08 electric vehicle appears at the company’s event in Beijing, China, April 8, 2026. REUTERS/Maxim Shemetov/File Photo Volkswagen didn’t comment on the sales forecasts in the documents. In a statement, the automaker said its partnership with Xpeng has delivered a new electric architecture to underpin locally made models and support faster vehicle development – a project it said was completed in a record 18 months. The UNYX 08 SUV and the related UNYX 09 sedan were additional outcomes of the tie-up, the company added. Xpeng (9868.HK) declined to comment. Problems with the UNYX 08 began with the vehicle itself. The car launched with a price tag of about $34,260. But similarly priced Chinese rivals offered more-sophisticated features. Xiaomi’s YU7 had an advanced sensor package; Zeekr's 7X offered fast charging. Xiaomi sold almost 57,000 YU7s and Zeekr sold more than 21,000 7Xs between April and August, compared with about 1,300 UNYX 08s, according to ThinkerCar. "Chinese customers ask: Why buy an expensive German car if they can get the technology much cheaper,” said Pedro Pacheco, vice president of research at Gartner. Stephen Reitman, an auto analyst at Bernstein, recalled that Volkswagen showed analysts computer renderings of the Xpeng-linked models in April 2024. "The next day we went to the Beijing auto show and you could basically see this kind of design already on the market," Reitman said. A distribution gamble compounded the product’s challenges, five people told Reuters. Volkswagen largely sold the UNYX 08 through a separate, new dealer network run by Volkswagen Anhui, an EV-focused venture, rather than the more than 3,000 dealerships Volkswagen operated with joint-venture partners FAW and SAIC (600104.SS) . Volkswagen Anhui’s far-smaller footprint meant many consumers were unaware the vehicle existed, two of the people said. Volkswagen said sales of the Anhui models, including the earlier UNYX 06 and 07, were growing. The unit had expanded its sales network to 166 outlets and was working with FAW-Volkswagen at selected dealerships, the company said, adding that this approach aimed to reach more customers. FAW and SAIC didn’t respond to questions. The XPeng logo is displayed on a tire of an XPeng GX SUV, on display at an XPeng dealership, in Beijing, China, April 23, 2026. REUTERS/Tingshu Wang/File Photo For Volkswagen, the Xpeng partnership follows a string of troubled ventures, missed opportunities and abandoned initiatives in China that spanned batteries, autonomous driving, charging infrastructure, software and even flying cars . Volkswagen was “too slow in building the competence they need today,” said Stefan Bratzel, founder and director of the Center of Automotive Management, a German research institute. The dilemma faces nearly every foreign automaker in China. Having fallen behind in software, batteries and vehicle platforms, foreign brands have turned to Chinese partners to stay in the game. Yet access to Chinese technology doesn’t guarantee they can match local rivals’ speed, execution or appeal with consumers. Chinese brands led by BYD and Geely have gained share by bringing software-rich vehicles to market faster and often at lower prices, forcing once-dominant rivals including Volkswagen and Toyota to [USN:L1N45707R TEXT:"fight for relevance"]. ANOTHER BIG BET Despite the UNYX 08’s weak reception, Volkswagen is setting similarly aggressive targets for its next model developed with Xpeng, the UNYX 09 sedan. The car is due to reach showrooms this month. Company product-planning documents earlier this year forecast average monthly sales of nearly 4,900 vehicles, with annual volume exceeding 90,000 by 2034. At Volkswagen, ambitious forecasts can be essential to securing approval for new models from Wolfsburg headquarters, which can incentivize managers to submit optimistic projections, according to two people familiar with its planning. Volkswagen logo at the carmaker's main German plant in Wolfsburg, Germany, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Liesa Johannssen/File Photo Volkswagen initially expected to sell 32,600 UNYX 08s through the end of 2026 and 70,400 next year, the planning documents show. Those plans, made in 2024, show the automaker also expected annual sales of more than 120,000 vehicles later in the product cycle. But early this year, Volkswagen cut the 2026 projection by more than 60% to 12,300 vehicles, the documents show. It nevertheless forecast sales of 64,000 in 2027, about 10% below the initial target. In recent weeks, the company has been advertising the UNYX 08 at a 17% discount on the April launch price. ‘MARRIAGE AND DIVORCE’ Volkswagen saw the Chinese disruption coming. At a 2019 presentation for investors and shareholders, Volkswagen Group China said it was preparing nearly 40 locally produced new-energy vehicle models — EVs and plug-in hybrids — by 2025 and could deliver 1.5 million in China that year. It achieved less than one-tenth of that target, delivering 115,500 battery-electric vehicles in China last year, according to company data. As China's EV market accelerated, Volkswagen explored various local tie-ups, hoping to unlock the speed and expertise it lacked, according to three people, corporate records and public announcements. Two people familiar with Volkswagen's China partnerships said the company called this approach "marriage and divorce" – forming alliances with local companies to learn from them, then exiting once it had absorbed what it needed. Around the time Ralf Brandstaetter became Volkswagen China's chief executive in August 2022, the automaker explored cooperation with BYD – China’s largest EV maker – including potentially using BYD's Dolphin platform for the Jetta brand, according to two people. Those efforts haven’t been previously reported. During due diligence, Volkswagen staff examining BYD's finances were struck by the Chinese automaker's lower manufacturing costs, one of the people said. BYD (002594.SZ) wasn’t interested in collaborating, the two sources said. Reuters couldn’t establish why a deal didn’t happen. Visitors check a BYD Seagull electric vehicle (EV) displayed at the Beijing International Automotive Exhibition, or Auto China, in Beijing, China April 26, 2026. REUTERS/Xiaoyu Yin/File Photo The Chinese EV maker would seize Volkswagen’s crown as China’s sales leader in 2023. That same year, Volkswagen also explored a partnership with Leapmotor (9863.HK) , according to the two people. Stellantis (STLAM.MI) ultimately [USN:L4N3BV66D TEXT:"struck a deal"] with Leapmotor later that year. Volkswagen’s statement didn’t address the BYD and Leapmotor talks. BYD didn’t comment, while Leapmotor didn’t respond to questions. Some partnerships that did materialize generated new problems rather than solving old ones. Reuters reported in July that Volkswagen's canceled flying-car project had become mired in legal disputes with a Chinese partner. A venture with Chinese startup Du-Power to build fast-charging stations also went awry. The tie-up, launched in 2020, ended in shareholder disputes, litigation and supplier complaints alleging unpaid bills, corporate filings show. In 2024, the startup sued Volkswagen China and the venture’s executives and directors, alleging harm to its business interests. Volkswagen told Reuters that China’s Supreme People’s Court dismissed the startup’s claims in March. Neither Du-Power nor the court responded to questions. ‘EXCEPTIONAL’ CONTRACTION In some ways, Volkswagen’s predicament illustrates the success of China's industrial policy. In exchange for market access, Volkswagen tied up with Chinese automakers, shared technology and invested — only to be outsold by local players. Those checkered bets are now colliding with a market in convulsion after years of breakneck growth. In a September 10 message to staff reviewed by Reuters, Brandstaetter described an industry facing an "exceptional" contraction. He said Volkswagen expected China’s passenger-car market to [USN:P8N43T0CN TEXT:"shrink by 20% this year"], or about 4.5 million vehicles. Ralf Brandstaetter, head of Volkswagen China business, and He Xiaopeng, founder and chief executive officer of XPeng, attend a Volkswagen media event in Beijing, China April 24, 2024. REUTERS/Josh Arslan/File Photo Brandstaetter said industry profit margins had fallen to 1.5%, product cycles had compressed from seven years to three, and new EV models were seeing steep sales declines after three months. Volkswagen, he wrote, must urgently "align our production capacities with market realities" and eliminate "unnecessary duplication" among China brands and entities — a reckoning with a crisis years in the making. In 2019, one in five passenger cars sold in China was a Volkswagen. In the first eight months of this year, the group’s share had fallen to 10%, according to the China Passenger Car Association. What distinguishes Volkswagen’s plight is its deep dependence on China and its struggle to execute a decisive transformation in a market now dominated by Chinese companies. That made its Xpeng bet pivotal. One former Volkswagen figure compared its predicament to that faced by Nokia, Kodak and BlackBerry: The automaker’s leadership assumed its brands would endure, even as the market shifted toward Chinese competitors with superior technology and faster innovation cycles. Bill Russo, founder of Shanghai-based advisory firm Automobility, sees the comparison as a useful warning but not yet a verdict. Volkswagen still has a path to recovery, he said. The risk, he added, “is that the market moves faster than the company can reinvent itself.”

item.title: Israel’s key election has high economic stakes
item.description: Israel’s economy has outperformed despite years of war. Yet under Benjamin Netanyahu’s far-right coalition, subsidies and benefits flow heavily to the Haredi minority, while native-born emigration jumped 60% from 2022 to 2024. A new government could reap an economic dividend.
item.dc:creator: Yawen Chen
item.content:encoded: Given that he was Israel's leader when around 1,200 people were killed in the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, Benjamin Netanyahu has a surprisingly good chance of performing well in next week's national elections. Part of that is down to the Israeli prime minister’s military campaigns, which have restored his standing in the eyes of some of his countrymen. It’s also because he presides over an economy that in 2025 managed to grow over a percentage point above the 1.8% average of members of the OECD club of developed countries. Even so, a different government might be able to claim an economic dividend. The violence and turmoil of the past three years make Israel's economic resilience striking. True, sovereign debt is heading towards 70% of GDP, up around 10 percentage points since 2022, and the fiscal deficit has risen to nearly 5% of GDP, from under 2%. But while defence spending has doubled to around 8% of GDP, higher military budgets overseas are boosting demand for drones and cyber systems made by the high-tech sector that constitutes over half of Israel’s exports. The Tel Aviv 125 Index (.TA125) has jumped over 130% in the past three years, beating the S&P 500 Index’s (.SPX) 80% rise, while the cost of insuring five-year Israeli government debt against default is roughly back to its September 2023 level. The central bank still holds $237 billion in foreign-exchange reserves, more than a third of GDP. Still, the country’s growth and tax revenues rest on a small number of people. High tech accounted for 18% of GDP in 2025 and half the economy’s growth. Yet workers in high-tech occupations, physicians and senior university academics together make up around 300,000 people, or about 3% of Israelis, according to Dan Ben-David of the independent Shoresh Institution for Socioeconomic Research . The top 20% of workers bring in 93% of the government's income-tax revenue, he says. Such concentration makes departures potentially costly. In 2024, 35,993 native-born Israelis emigrated, 62% above the annual average between 2009 and 2022, while only 13,820 returned. More recent data points the same way. During the second half of 2025, 35% of surveyed high-tech companies reported an increase in relocation requests, while Israeli R&D employment fell for the first time in a decade, the Israel Innovation Authority says. Israeli startups inevitably expand abroad and hire closer to customers. But there is evidence that politics has influenced relocation decisions by at least some of the highly skilled Israelis the country wants to retain. Netanyahu’s government in 2023 sought greater political influence over judicial appointments and limits on the Supreme Court’s powers, sparking huge street protests. Supporters said judges had accumulated excessive authority, but opponents warned the changes would weaken checks on executive power. Parliament last year approved [USN:L2N3QB06G TEXT:"legislation"] giving politicians greater sway over judicial appointments, with the changes due to take effect after the next election. Rivka Carmi, a former Israeli university president who chairs ScienceAbroad, says a survey of Israeli researchers overseas in August 2023 found more than half were considering remaining abroad, compared with about 6% who said that had been their intention when they originally left. She says concern over the government’s judicial overhaul was a major factor. War has added to those pressures. A follow-up ScienceAbroad survey in 2024 found security and the conflict had become important considerations alongside domestic politics. Carmi says some Israelis overseas are “sitting on their suitcases”, waiting to see who wins the election and whether any change lasts. The broader verdict on Netanyahu’s recent military activities is mixed at home too. Israel says it moved into Gaza to dismantle Hamas after the October 7 attacks, but the campaign has devastated much of the enclave and drawn widespread international criticism. A September survey by Israel’s Institute for National Security Studies, an independent security-policy think tank, found only 34% Israelis were satisfied with the government’s handling of the Gaza war, though 61% were satisfied with that of the military. Just 27% said Israel had won the Gaza campaign, while 23% said it had prevailed against Iran. The external fallout creates another problem. A Pew survey this year found on average 67% of adults across 36 countries viewed Israel unfavourably, including 60% in the United States. That worsening international sentiment matters for a technology sector whose success depends heavily on access to global capital and markets. Another, potentially larger, economic fault line is the ultra-Orthodox community known as the Haredi. Only 53% of Haredi men were employed in 2025 , compared with about 87% of non-Haredi Jewish men, because a large share remain in full-time religious study. Government support has often reinforced that model, with funding for ultra-Orthodox institutions forming part of coalition bargaining. Shoresh estimates that subsidies and benefits to the Haredi community from central and local governments totalled 37.5 billion shekels ($12.1 billion) in 2024, exceeding the 26.7 billion shekels the central government spent on hospitals, universities and colleges combined. Many Haredi men have also historically received exemptions from conscription . Demographic trends raises the cost of that imbalance. In 2023, Haredim made up only about 6% of Israelis aged 50 to 54, but 26% of children under 5. As that generation enters adulthood, its employment and productivity will increasingly determine Israel’s ability to finance the state. A new government could require more members of this community to work and serve in the military. It could also educate its populace better. Many Haredi boys do not study the full core curriculum, including subjects such as maths and English. Arab Israelis, who make up about a fifth of the population, also receive significantly poorer educational outcomes. Higher defence spending makes a broader tax base more urgent. Without stronger employment and productivity growth elsewhere, Israel will have to choose between leaning still more heavily on the narrow group already providing much of its tax revenue, accepting higher debt, or squeezing spending elsewhere. That raises the stakes of the election. Four recent polls put Netanyahu’s bloc on between 49 and 53 seats and the main opposition bloc on between 50 and 54, leaving both short of the 61 needed for a majority. Israel held five elections between 2019 and 2022, so another inconclusive result is possible. The economy’s relative resilience should cushion any near-term impact. In the longer term, however, Israelis’ choice could lead to two very distinct outcomes. Follow Yawen Chen on Bluesky and LinkedIn . Israel is set to hold a national election on October 27. item.title: Daiwa, Mizuho clear final hurdles to launch China securities units, Bloomberg says
item.description: Japanese banks Mizuho Financial Group and Daiwa Securities are poised to launch fully independent securities operations in China after clearing crucial regulatory hurdles, according to a Bloomberg report.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japanese banks Mizuho Financial Group (8411.T) and Daiwa Securities (8601.T) are poised to launch fully independent securities operations in China after clearing crucial regulatory hurdles, according to a Bloomberg report. The move highlights expansion efforts by Japanese financial companies in China, setting them apart from several Western competitors grappling with prolonged waits for such permits. Both institutions were recently notified that they had successfully passed final reviews for such operations on the mainland, the report said, citing a source familiar with the matter. Mizuho and Daiwa did not immediately respond to requests for comment. China’s financial regulators did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. The move caps long-running efforts by both institutions to build up their onshore presence. In September last year Mizuho [USN:L2N3VH0JE TEXT:"won the securities licence"] in China needed to secure a green light from regulators for operations in the domestic market. It officially [USN:P8N3C101E TEXT:"applied"] to set up its unit in November 2023. Daiwa, which has been consolidating operational control, agreed this year to [USN:L1N40T03J TEXT:"buy out"] local joint venture partners in a $100 million deal to pave the way for a wholly owned structure. While Japanese institutions secure their green lights, major US banking peers are navigating uncertainty while waiting for Beijing's final go-ahead. Citigroup (C.N) has been waiting for clearance since it applied late in 2021 for a wholly-owned mainland brokerage license, while market maker Citadel Securities, with an application pending since early 2025, also awaits the nod.

item.title: As Japan pursues a chip-industry reboot, it's being pressed to build America's
item.description: Japan is in the midst of a major push to revive its chip sector, but its latest investments show how Tokyo is being pulled into helping the US build up its own semiconductor industry.
item.dc:creator: Kentaro Okasaka, Tamiyuki Kihara
item.content:encoded: Japan is in the midst of a major push to revive its chip sector, but its latest investments show how Tokyo is being pulled into helping the US build up its own semiconductor industry. Japan will invest up to $21 billion to build two chip factories in New York state, under a deal announced last week by GlobalFoundries (GFS.O) , which is majority-owned by Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund, Mubadala Investment Co. It is part of a pledge to invest $550 billion in the US made with the Trump administration in return for lower tariffs. Under that deal, the US president - not Japan - gets to select the projects. That shows the price Japan is paying to maintain trade relations with the US, the world's largest economy and its closest security partner. But the pledge, agreed to in July 2025, will not do much to resurrect Japan's chip industry and will have a limited impact on improving its supply chain resilience, experts said. "Japan is funding US semiconductor capacity without necessarily gaining much of the advanced chip technology or domestic manufacturing capabilities it wants," said Nori Chiou, investment director at White Oak Capital. US President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on countries around the world last year to try to shrink the US trade deficit, with governments in South Korea and Taiwan also making investment pledges. It is not the first time that Japan has been pushed around by the US over chips. In the 1980s, Japan - the globally dominant chipmaking centre - agreed to restrict semiconductor exports to the US, with memories of that period remaining a sore point for bureaucrats in Tokyo. "Investment in the US is, ultimately, a measure for dealing with Trump. It is essentially about buying time in order to maintain the US-Japan relationship," said a Japanese government source, who declined to be named as the issue is politically contentious. INDISPENSABLE PARTNER Earlier this month, Japanese industry minister Ryosei Akazawa, when asked if corporate investment in the US could weaken investment in Japan, said: "We believe that investment in the US and domestic growth investment are entirely compatible." "Japan is a partner the US cannot do without to maintain its supremacy as a hegemonic power in economic, security and technological terms," Akazawa said last week. He negotiated the investment pledge in a previous role. The investment will benefit Japanese equipment manufacturers like Tokyo Electron (8035.T) , whose earnings have swelled due to the AI boom, while customers will include Renesas Electronics (6723.T) , GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen has said. Tokyo needs to arrange financing for the chip factories, with other previously announced projects including oil and natural gas-related investments and small nuclear reactors. The state-backed Japan Bank for International Cooperation and commercial banks will provide loans, with guarantees from Nippon Export and Investment Insurance. Japanese banks have been reluctant to participate due to the cost of acquiring the large amount of US dollars required, with Tokyo looking to JPMorgan and other US banks for help, Reuters has reported. Japan is hardly flush with cash, with the highest debt-to-GDP ratio in the developed world and investor concerns about Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's fiscal expansion plans. REGARD INVESTMENT AS A TAX Takaichi has ambitions to pour public-private investment totalling some $2.3 trillion through fiscal 2040 across 17 strategic Japanese sectors, including AI and chips. As economic security has become front of mind, the government's thinking has shifted to the view that having a manufacturing base in Japan is extremely important, said a government source who declined to be named because the matter is politically contentious. Japan's flagship chip-sector project is Rapidus, which seeks to mass-produce cutting-edge chips starting next year but is widely viewed with scepticism by the industry. Tokyo is also backing robot AI company Noetra and has provided subsidies to TSMC (2330.TW) , Micron (MU.O) and Kioxia (285A.T) to locate chipmaking capacity in Japan. If US-made chips can be integrated into Japan's semiconductor supply chain, there is no need for everything to be produced domestically, the first government source said. "Whether (the chip factory investment) works out or not, Japan will just have to regard it as a tax," said Atsushi Osanai, a professor at Waseda University.

item.title: Two-run homers send Rays past Guardians in Game 6, into World Series
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays are headed back to the World Series, 18 years to the day since they captured the first American League pennant in franchise history.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- The Tampa Bay Rays are headed back to the World Series, 18 years to the day since they captured the first American League pennant in franchise history. Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz each belted a two-run homer, helping Tampa Bay advance to the World Series for the third time in franchise history with a 7-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians on Monday. The Rays recorded their third straight win to capture the American League Championship Series in six games. Tampa Bay will visit Milwaukee for Game 1 of the World Series on Friday. The Brewers won two of the three games against the visiting Rays in the regular season in a series played March 30-April 1. Tampa Bay was unsuccessful in its previous two trips to the Fall Classic. The Rays fell in five games to the Philadelphia Phillies in 2008 and in six games to the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2020. Caminero celebrated his first career postseason homer by emphatically slapping his chest before rounding first base and posing with his arms folded at home plate. The latter gesture was a nod to former Tampa Bay slugger Randy Arozarena, who was in the crowd on Monday at Tropicana Field. "Tampa, this is for you," Caminero screamed during his postgame interview with TNT Sports, doing his best LeBron James imitation after the latter helped the Cleveland Cavaliers win the 2016 NBA Finals. Diaz, who guaranteed after Game 5 that "we're going to win tomorrow," provided the exclamation point in the eighth inning on Monday with a homer over the left field wall. "A lot of people didn't believe me, but here are the results," Diaz said of predicting the Game 6 victory. Diaz was signed by Cleveland in 2013 out of Cuba and traded to Tampa Bay in 2018. Caminero was signed by Cleveland in 2019 out of the Dominican Republic and traded to Tampa Bay in 2021. Tampa Bay's Richie Palacios, who also began his career with Cleveland, laced a two-run double into the right-center-field gap in the second inning to open the scoring. That was enough offense for Freddy Peralta (2-0), who allowed one run on five hits and three walks while striking out three in 5 1/3 innings. He went 2-0 in three appearances (two starts) during the series, yielding one run on nine hits in 12 innings while striking out nine to earn ALCS MVP honors. "This is for the boys," Peralta said after being presented with the award. Cleveland's Nathaniel Lowe had an RBI single in the sixth inning, and Rays reliever Ian Seymour issued a bases-loaded walk to Patrick Bailey and then hit Angel Martinez with his next pitch to trim Tampa Bay's lead to 5-3 in the eighth. Kevin Kelly relieved Seymour and struck out Brayan Rocchio on three pitches to end the inning. After Diaz's blast restored the Rays' four-run lead, Bryan Baker retired the side in order in the ninth to end the game. "Let it hurt. Let it sink in. Let it fuel you this winter," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said of his message to his players. Caminero chased Cleveland opener Shawn Armstrong (0-1) with a single to lead off the second inning. Chandler Simpson reached on a fielder's choice off Tim Herrin and promptly stole second base. Victor Mesa Jr. walked before both runners advanced a base and later scored on Palacios' double. Armstrong allowed one run on one hit in one-plus innings. Herrin permitted one run on one hit in two-thirds of an inning. Tampa Bay tacked on in the third inning when Caminero scored on Jonny DeLuca's sacrifice fly for a 3-0 lead. --Field Level Media

item.title: Promoter challenges decision in WBA lightweight title bout over 'officiating errors'
item.description: Boxing promoter Most Valuable Promotions has challenged the decision to award Floyd Schofield a unanimous victory over Lucas Bahdi in their WBA lightweight title bout in Chicago this month, saying significant officiating errors impacted the outcome.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Boxing promoter Most Valuable Promotions has challenged the decision to award Floyd Schofield a unanimous victory over Lucas Bahdi in their WBA lightweight title bout in Chicago this month, saying significant officiating errors impacted the outcome. American Schofield came out a 115-111, 116-110, 119-108 winner on the judges' scorecards on October 10. He was left on the canvas after tangling with Canadian Bahdi in the third, sixth and ninth rounds, but the referee did not rule those as knockdowns. "The video evidence demonstrates multiple significant officiating errors that directly impacted the outcome of the fight," Most Valuable Promotions said in a statement on Monday. "Our review shows that had these knockdowns been properly ruled and scored, Lucas would have won the WBA lightweight world championship by majority decision. "We have a responsibility to advocate for our fighters, especially when a world championship is at stake." Schofield's promoter Golden Boy Promotions and the World Boxing Association did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside regular business hours in North America.

AI infrastructure company Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) sank nearly 30% below its initial public offering price on Tuesday, while the tech-heavy KOSPI (.KS11) gauge lost nearly 4%, showing shaky sentiment after a market selloff that derailed some deals. Along with quarterly results, the massive [USN:L8N4651G6 TEXT:"spending plans"] of the major AI players are increasingly in focus. Facebook operator Meta Platforms (META.O) , due to report on Wednesday, is one of five AI hyperscalers expected to increase combined capital expenditure to about $1.2 trillion next year, according to Goldman Sachs. As infrastructure plans grow ever larger and borrowing costs soar, investors are questioning "whether every dollar of AI capex earns more than it costs to finance," said Ninghui Liu, head of investment strategy and research for APAC at State Street Investment Management. On the docket today, Netflix (NFLX.O) is expected to report slowing revenue growth in the third quarter, while SpaceX (SPCX.O) is forecast to report $12.74 billion in quarterly revenue. General Motors (GM.N) , Hasbro (HAS.O) , Halliburton (HAL.N) , and 3M (MMM.N) are among the more-established names due to report on Tuesday. Oil prices resumed their [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"climb"] on Tuesday as it seemed unclear whether US President Donald Trump would go through with a waiver of [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"sanctions"] on some Russian energy exports, while fresh [USN:L1N46509O TEXT:"violence"] in the Middle East heightened the risk of supply disruptions. Inflationary pressures from elevated oil prices have put most major central banks on a tightening bias, though with a careful eye on whether economies are resilient enough to absorb higher interest rates. Recent comments from Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Kevin Warsh, suggest policymakers are in no rush to hike rates again. European Central Bank policymaker Martin Kocher is due to speak later on Tuesday, as well as ECB policymaker and Finnish central bank governor Olli Rehn. item.title: Coach of England's test team should be English, says New Zealander Fleming
item.description: Stephen Fleming is the fifth foreign coach to take charge of England's test team but the New Zealander hopes his successors will be English and says he will seek to develop home-grown coaching talent during his tenure.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Stephen Fleming is the fifth foreign coach to take charge of England's test team but the New Zealander hopes his successors will be English and says he will seek to develop home-grown coaching talent during his tenure. Fleming [USN:L1N43W0FU TEXT:"was appointed in July"] to replace compatriot Brendon McCullum, with Australian Trevor Bayliss and Zimbabwe's Duncan Fletcher and Andy Flower the other foreign coaches to have been at the helm of the test side. "I do believe that primarily the national team should be coached by a national representative," Fleming told the BBC in a podcast released on Monday. "I'm grateful for the opportunity, but there will be some development in terms of the coaching, and you can see by our staff," added the 53-year-old, who named former England players Marcus Trescothick, Richard Dawson and James Foster among his backroom staff last week. Fleming also highlighted the importance of having a good working relationship with former New Zealand teammate McCullum, who remains in charge of England's limited-overs team, with the Ashes and Cricket World Cup looming next year. "At some stage you're going to have to give up some of your key assets. We look at what's coming up, there's a test series for us against South Africa," he said. "We then move to the Ashes, which is obviously the milestone event for the summer next year, and then there's the World Cup. "Making sure that the players are as fit as can be for each of those marquee events and that we turn out good sides is going to be a challenge." England visit South Africa in a three-test series beginning in December.

item.title: Europe's earnings boom widens beyond energy and AI
item.description: European companies are expected to deliver another quarter of exceptional earnings growth, again driven mainly by profits at energy companies and those pivotal to the datacentre buildout, although signs are emerging of strength elsewhere.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Indyk
item.content:encoded: European companies are expected to deliver another quarter of exceptional earnings growth, again driven mainly by profits at energy companies and those pivotal to the datacentre buildout, although signs are emerging of strength elsewhere. Third-quarter earnings for the pan-regional STOXX 600 (.STOXX) are expected to grow 20.7% from a year ago, according to LSEG I/B/E/S, a slowdown from the second-quarter pace of 24%, but still among the fastest in years. With over half of the index's market capitalisation reporting over the next two weeks, here is what you need to know as the earnings season begins: 1/ WHERE ARE THE DOWNGRADES? In the past, analysts have typically cut earnings estimates ahead of reporting season. This time, in aggregate, they have raised forecasts, suggesting better-than-expected growth, optimism over AI spending and elevated energy prices will lead to stronger profit growth. "Some of these dynamics look a little different than usual," David Groman, global equity strategist at Citi, said, adding they were "unseasonably strong and unusually broad". Pre-earnings upgrades could make investors focus less on whether companies beat their third-quarter estimates and more on their outlook for the fourth quarter and beyond for clues on whether momentum can continue. 2/ ALL ABOUT AI Europe lacks AI big-hitters, such as Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) or Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) , but it has many smaller hardware stocks, materials and industrials that are benefiting from the capex boom. Tech earnings are forecast to increase by almost 33% from a year ago, according to LSEG I/B/E/S, while industrials profits are expected to rise by 11%. "It's often said Europe doesn't really have any AI plays but we think you can pick through French and German industrials," said Dorian Carrell, head of multi-asset income at Schroders. "Expectations there have been tempered over the last few weeks, but there is a chance for European industrials to surpass expectations." 3/ ENERGY BOOST The rise in oil and gas prices internationally since the outbreak of the US-Iran war has increased inflation and is a cost for many, but it has also boosted earnings expectations for companies that can benefit. "The big reason for the continued upgrades for earnings this year in Europe has been the tailwind from energy prices," Barclays equity strategists said. That support could fade if tensions in the Middle East ease and energy prices retreat, or if sustained high prices curb demand, turning the energy sector from a boost to a drag on broader earnings growth. "We expect refining-geared names to outperform, and we think the question now is: how long this lasts," Barclays added. 4/ BANKING BOUNCE? Europe's banks, one of the best-performing sectors in global equities over the last four years, have come under pressure from political concerns, but analysts do not anticipate a poor earnings season. Europe's bank index (.SX7P) is down 7% since the start of September, compared to a 1.7% drop for the broader STOXX 600, offering a lower bar to clear. The sector trades at about 10 times its forward earnings, which are expected to grow at about 8% over the medium term, a backdrop that should support the sector going forward, according to Schroders' Carrell, especially as recent volatility has depressed expectations. "The capital positions are strong, but the key thing is the lending activity picking up," Carrell said. "Everything points to European banks being in a good place." 5/ CONSUMER RESILIENCE Worries about consumers lacking spending power have lingered in Europe for years, but Maximilian Uleer, head of European equity and cross-asset strategy at Deutsche Bank, is upbeat. Trading at 13.6 times forward earnings, Europe's consumer staples sector (.S600CSP) trades at a 35% discount to its US counterpart, which Uleer thinks is too low. "I prefer European staples over US staples, because of the valuation difference and similar earnings profile," Uleer said. The European staples sector is expected to grow earnings by over 7% in the third quarter. "There's good reason to believe that the consumer is more resilient than we think, especially in Europe, and that's why we like staples. I think people will be surprised by more positive numbers."

item.title: Too much of a good scent? Hanoi curbs iconic trees
item.description: Vietnam's capital Hanoi has launched a large-scale programme to prune hundreds of its iconic blackboard trees and is considering relocating some after their distinctive fragrance proved too much for some residents.
item.dc:creator: Khanh Vu, Phuong Nguyen
item.content:encoded: Vietnam's capital Hanoi has launched a large-scale programme to prune hundreds of its iconic blackboard trees and is considering relocating some after their distinctive fragrance proved too much for some residents. Known in Vietnamese as hoa sua, meaning "milk flower", and also known as pulai and devil's tree elsewhere in Asia, blackboard trees can grow as tall as 60 metres (197 feet). The name reflects the traditional use of its wood for school items, as does its scientific name, Alstonia scholaris. Blackboard trees have lined Hanoi's boulevards since they were introduced during French colonial rule in the late 19th century. They were later planted across the capital, and Hanoi now has about 14,400 of the trees, according to the city government. At dusk, the trees release a pungent, sweet scent from their greenish-white flowers, peaking in September and October. Long associated with the arrival of autumn in Hanoi, they have inspired hit songs and poetry for decades. But many of the city's nearly 9 million residents say the fragrance is overpowering. "I simply cannot stand the smell," said Hanoi resident Nguyen Ha Long, 43, who said he stopped his evening runs because the scent gave him migraines. TRIMMING 7% OF TREES After years of complaints and smaller interventions, local authorities have launched their largest pruning campaign yet, stripping the flowers from about 7% of Hanoi's blackboard trees during a five-day blitz ending on Tuesday. Officials also plan to relocate trees from streets where they are most heavily concentrated, adding to the impact of major public works projects underway in Hanoi that are rapidly reshaping the city's landscape as the ruling Communist Party chases ultra-fast economic growth. Not everybody backs the move. "I absolutely love the scent of blackboard trees. The stronger the fragrance, the more I love it," said Nguyen Thu Trang, 37, who lives on central Nguyen Du, a street lined with blackboard trees and which was also the setting of the best-selling novel "The Sorrow of War". "My family has lived here for over 30 years, and we all love the scent. I feel deeply saddened seeing the city prune them," she added. "The smell is not toxic," said Tran Cong Khanh, head of Vietnam's ethnomedicine research centre, echoing views expressed by three other Vietnamese scientists interviewed by Reuters, who however recommend limiting concentrations in densely populated areas because the pollen, like that of other plants, can trigger allergic reactions. The debate has been widely reported by local newspapers, despite public health rarely ranking among Vietnamese residents' top concerns. By contrast, air pollution, which often makes Hanoi one of the [USN:L5N3FR0LA TEXT:"world's most polluted cities "]during winter, has generally attracted less public attention.

item.title: Sea plans IPO for financial services arm Monee, memo says
item.description: Singapore-headquartered tech conglomerate Sea Limited is planning a public listing for its financial services arm Monee and will also launch an AI enterprise platform business, according to an internal memo sent on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Singapore-headquartered tech conglomerate Sea Limited (SE.N) is planning a public listing for its financial services arm Monee and will also launch an AI enterprise platform business, according to an internal memo sent on Tuesday. Founder Forrest Li, in a memo to employees that was reviewed by Reuters, said he believed going public would give its financial payments and services business the "resources and the room to go further and faster than it can today”. The business operates in Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines, Taiwan, and Brazil and offers mobile wallets, payments processing, credit, and banking services. Sea did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The memo said the tech group would also launch an AI-first enterprise platform named Sea Cloud. In the memo, which was sent on the ninth anniversary of the group’s public listing in New York, Li said the quarterly revenue for the group had grown more than 80 times over that period to $7.8 billion. (This story has been corrected to change the spelling of the founder's name to 'Li,' not 'Lee,' in paragraphs 2 and 6.)

item.title: Software upgrades eat nearly a third of companies' IT budgets, survey finds
item.description: Large US and British companies spend 28% of their software budgets on average to pay for vendor-driven upgrades, migration and licensing changes they would not have actively chosen, adding avoidable costs and operational risks in the race to adopt AI solutions, a survey by software maintenance provider Origina showed on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Anastasiia Kozlova
item.content:encoded: Large US and British companies spend 28% of their software budgets on average to pay for vendor-driven upgrades, migration and licensing changes they would not have actively chosen, adding avoidable costs and operational risks in the race to adopt AI solutions, a survey by software maintenance provider Origina showed on Tuesday. These hard-to-avoid recurring costs and operational disruption were described as a "software tax" in the study that surveyed more than 2,000 companies. "When the alternative to an unwanted upgrade is losing support on systems the business runs on, saying yes is often a rational response," Origina CEO Tomas O'Leary said. 95% of respondents said they had paid for a vendor-driven upgrade they expected to worsen outcomes, while 80% said leaving a major software vendor would significantly disrupt their business 84% said senior engineering staff "always" or "often" devoted time to vendor-driven software changes rather than innovation or business-focused development 91% said they had retired fully functional hardware in the past three years to comply with vendors' support deadlines, sacrificing 1.65 years of remaining useful life on average O'Leary said the issue was largely universal and also applied to other regions, with older companies with more entrenched technology stacks facing the biggest challenges According to the report, the most recent vendor-driven software change resulted in an average annual cost of $12.87 million for the surveyed organizations (This story has been corrected to say 'vendor-driven,' not 'vendor-mandated,' in the second bullet point.)

item.title: Rubio kicks off India visit with trade deal, Russian oil on agenda
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India on Tuesday, days after President Donald Trump delayed tariffs on US imports from the world's largest democracy as the two countries seek to finalize a trade deal.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to India on Tuesday, days after President Donald Trump delayed tariffs on US imports from the world's largest democracy as the two countries seek to finalize a trade deal. During the two-day visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar in western India, Rubio is slated to meet government and business leaders, including Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and billionaire Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which operates the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar. Rubio and other officials have said in recent days that a comprehensive trade deal between the two nations is almost complete, raising the possibility that it could be signed during the secretary's visit. Trump removed one potential stumbling block last Friday when he waived potential tariffs that would have punished New Delhi for the nation's extensive Russian crude oil purchases. Under legislation signed by Trump in September, the administration is authorized to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil, which would include India, which is number two on that list after China. Trump's decision to waive all substantive provisions of that bill has upset both Democrats and Republicans who have pushed him to up economic pressure on Moscow for its war with Ukraine. Rubio has said in recent days that the effort to finalize a trade deal was a factor in the decision to waive those tariffs. He also said that India has been diversifying its import mix away from Russian crude, even as it still buys millions of barrels of Russian oil every day. He said the administration was entering a 60-day review period, during which it would consider which new tariffs, if any, to enact. "You've got countries like India, for example, that have voluntarily diversified their energy portfolio, but are still getting a substantial amount of energy from Russia because it's hard to pivot from one day to the next," Rubio said on Sunday. "But they're also an important ally and partner of the United States." While the Trump administration has in the past pressed India to cut Russian oil imports, the US signed a deal with Russia last week to import diesel to bring down domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections, making it unclear to what extent that remains a foreign policy priority. "Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account," Rubio told reporters on Monday when asked about India's Russian oil purchases. "Geography is real. For some countries, it's very difficult to acquire energy from alternative sources." India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements to help power its fast-growing economy. Rubio is slated to fly into Mumbai from Samarkand, Uzbekistan, where he was meeting with Central Asian political and business leaders.

item.title: How safe havens stack up as tech, energy and France fears grip markets
item.description: Demand for safe-haven assets is strong as AI jitters hurt tech stocks, the Iran war continues and keeps energy prices elevated, while worries about high government debt loads persist.
item.dc:creator: Sophie Kiderlin, Canan Sevgili, Sruthi Shankar
item.content:encoded: Demand for safe-haven assets is strong as [USN:L6N461185 TEXT:"AI jitters"] hurt tech stocks, the Iran war continues and keeps energy prices elevated, while worries about high government debt loads persist. Yet traditional safe havens have not performed as well as expected this year: Gold sold off after the start of the Iran war as investors ditched [USN:L4N3ZR1OA TEXT:"top-performing assets"] given losses elsewhere. Government bonds, once considered one of the world's safest assets, [USN:L1N462089 TEXT:"are volatile"].
