item.title: GCash owner Mynt edges higher in record Philippine IPO amid Asian selloff
item.description: Shares of fintech firm Mynt , operator of mobile wallet GCash, rose 1.7% in their market debut on Tuesday after the company raised 60.9 billion pesos ($966.99 million) in the largest-ever initial public offering in the Philippines.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Karen Lema, Roshan Thomas
item.content:encoded: Shares of fintech firm Mynt (GCASH.PS) , operator of mobile wallet GCash, rose 1.7% in their market debut on Tuesday after the company raised 60.9 billion pesos ($966.99 million) in the largest-ever initial public offering in the Philippines. The stock opened at 6.63 pesos a share, up from its offer price of 6.60 pesos, before rising further to 6.71 pesos. The broader Philippine Stock Exchange index (.PSI) was down 0.02%. The firm's debut demonstrated investor demand for Mynt's payments business even as a [USN:L4N466020 TEXT:"broader selloff"] in AI-related shares made investors more selective about new tech listings. "It is a record and, more importantly, a statement of confidence in Mynt, in the Philippine economy and in the strength of our capital market," Philippine Stock Exchange President and Chief Executive Officer Ramon Monzon said. Mynt's listing came as South Korean AI firm Elice [USN:L1N466008 TEXT:"fell sharply"] in its market debut on Tuesday, highlighting a more cautious mood toward companies tied to the AI boom. Mynt President and CEO Martha Sazon said the listing marked a new stage in the company's effort to widen access to financial services for Filipinos who have long been outside the formal banking system. Nearly 90% of GCash customers come from low- to middle-income households, she said. Mynt, backed by Globe Telecom (GLO.PS) , Ant Group and Ayala Corp (AC.PS) , owns GCash, the Philippines' largest finance app, according to its prospectus. The platform offers payments, money transfers, lending, savings, investments and insurance products. The company had 41.5 million monthly active users in the three-month period that ended on June 30, or nearly 56% of the Philippines' adult population, according to its prospectus. GCash users completed payment transactions worth 9.84 trillion pesos in the first half of 2026. BIGGEST IN THE PHILIPPINES Mynt's IPO surpassed Monde Nissin's (MONDE.PS) 52.2-billion-peso IPO in 2021 to become the largest-ever IPO in the Philippines, according to data compiled by LSEG. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said the listing came at a time when the stock market needed renewed investor interest and broader participation, adding that attracting fresh capital remained a challenge. He said strong demand from local and international investors offered a "reason for optimism" and reflected continued confidence in Filipino enterprises. The Mynt IPO attracted more than 20 cornerstone investors, who committed about $500 million, or nearly 60% of the base deal, according to the company. Investors included BlackRock, Citadel, Fidelity International and the International Finance Corp. Mynt sold 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos each. The exercise of an overallotment option increased the deal size to 60.9 billion pesos from 53 billion pesos. Mynt plans to use the proceeds to fund growth in its digital financial services business, product development and general corporate purposes, according to its prospectus. Mynt said that for the six-month period that ended on June 30, its net income rose 7.3% from a year earlier to 10.82 billion pesos. Revenue rose 10.4% to 43.27 billion pesos. ($1 = 62.9790 Philippine pesos)

item.title: Gold inches up on softer dollar as investors assess Fed rate outlook
item.description: Gold inched higher on Tuesday, helped by a softer US dollar, as market participants looked ahead to next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting for clues on the future path of interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Sukanya Mitra
item.content:encoded: Gold inched higher on Tuesday, helped by a softer US dollar, as market participants looked ahead to next week's Federal Reserve policy meeting for clues on the future path of interest rates. Spot gold was up 0.1% at $4,145.22 per ounce by 0347 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.1% to $4,164.70. "The interesting dynamic is that there's going to be a big move, no matter what the Fed does, and the initial reaction... might be supportive of gold if they keep interest rates unchanged," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. Recent comments from [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Fed"] officials signalling little [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"urgency"] for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting. According to CME's FedWatch Tool, traders are pricing in an 82% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged next week, but expectations for a hike in December remain at 89%. Higher interest rates typically weigh on gold prices because they increase the opportunity cost of holding bullion, which does not pay interest. The US dollar index (.DXY) softened on Tuesday, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for buyers overseas. Rodda said a de-escalation of tensions in the Middle East and a decline in oil prices could provide a further boost to gold prices. Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a [USN:L1N46601X TEXT:"five-month high"] as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis [USN:S8N44M08Y TEXT:"said on Monday"] they carried out several attacks against Saudi energy, airport and military targets. Elsewhere, [USN:L1N465004 TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] Governor Kazuo Ueda said underlying inflation is "quite close" to the central bank's 2% target, with strong global AI demand adding to inflationary pressure from a tight job market, signalling scope for further rate increases. Among other metals, spot silver rose 0.7% to $57.48 per ounce, platinum gained 0.7% to $1,651.25 and palladium fell 0.2% to $1,117.87.

item.title: In search for Amelia Earhart's plane, tantalizing clue turns out to be tree debris
item.description: US-based explorers who voyaged to a tiny South Pacific island seeking to solve conclusively the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart have determined that an object they suspected was wreckage from her plane was a cluster of washed-up trees.
item.dc:creator: Steve Gorman
item.content:encoded: US-based explorers who voyaged to a tiny South Pacific island seeking to solve conclusively the 1937 disappearance of famed aviator Amelia Earhart have determined that an object they suspected was wreckage from her plane was a cluster of washed-up trees. Leaders of the mission made the announcement on Monday. The [USN:L1N45S045 TEXT:"team set out"] this month from Los Angeles for the archipelago nation of Kiribati on a $900,000 expedition backed by private donors and Indiana's Purdue University, long affiliated with Earhart and her legacy. The objective was to learn whether an elongated, multi-pronged object detected by 2020 satellite imagery in the island's lagoon was a remnant of Earhart's long-missing twin-engine Lockheed Electra 10-E airplane. Such a finding would have decisively proven some scholars' hypothesis that Earhart and her navigator, Fred Noonan, crash-landed on or near the coral-ringed atoll and perished as castaways there, hundreds of miles from their intended refueling stop. 'ADVENTURE IS WORTHWHILE' "Unfortunately, we weren't able to find that smoking gun," Purdue general counsel and team member Steve Schultz said in a video message recorded on the island of Nikumaroro, part of the Phoenix Islands in Kiribati. Quoting Earhart, he added: "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself.'" After a week at the island, the team ultimately concluded that the "visual anomaly" picked up by satellite "was likely a collection of large trees" wedged in the sand at the lagoon, the expedition said in a statement. Much of that debris had fragmented and washed away since it was first spotted, leaving a smaller Y-shaped segment whose reflective surface - suggestive of metal - turned out to come from "its carbonate veneer," the team said in a statement. Two previous attempts to locate the aircraft's wreckage in the ocean around Nikumaroro also proved fruitless, and a plane-shaped sonar image captured elsewhere on the sea floor turned out to be a pile of rocks. Earhart and Noonan were last seen taking off in the Electra on July 2, 1937, from Papua New Guinea, during Earhart's multi-stage attempt to become the first woman to pilot a plane around the world, and the first aviator to circumnavigate the equator. Radio contact with the flight was lost the next day after Earhart, 39, reported "gas is running low," followed by her final known transmission giving her navigational line of position. CASTAWAY HYPOTHESIS 'REMAINS VERY STRONG' The disappearance spawned one of the largest air-sea searches ever undertaken, and endures as one of the great unsolved mysteries of the 20th century and aviation history. The expedition's leader, Richard Pettigrew, head of the Archaeological Legacy Institute of Eugene, Oregon, said evidence supporting the "castaway hypothesis," suggesting Earhart and Noonan died while marooned on Nikumaroro, "remains very strong." He cited the body of evidence collected during the past 30-plus years by veteran Earhart explorer Ric Gillespie, co-founder of The International Group for Historic Aircraft Recovery and author of the 2024 book "One More Good Flight: The Amelia Earhart Tragedy." His case includes multiple radio distress calls picked up in the days immediately after Earhart vanished with bearings that converge on Nikumaroro, and a 2018 forensic analysis of human bones recovered on the island in 1940 showing they belonged to a woman of Earhart's build and stature. Gillespie's investigation also encompassed such artifacts from the island as a woman's shoe, a compact case, a freckle cream jar and medicine vial, all dating to the 1930s, as well as remnants of a jackknife like one Earhart carried on the plane. Yet another piece of evidence is a photograph taken of the island's shoreline months after Earhart vanished showing an object that appears to be the Electra's landing gear. The Purdue expedition this month said it uncovered a number of other artifacts, including a steel tube 30 inches long found in the lagoon, that may yield additional evidence when studied. According to Gillespie, the plane has been lost to history, eventually swept by tides off the coral flat where it had landed and carried into the sea to sink and break apart in the surf. The official US government view of Earhart's fate has long been that her plane ran out of fuel and crashed at sea near its refueling destination of Howland Island, another dot of land about 400 miles (640 kilometers) northwest of Nikumaroro.

item.title: China leaves loan rates steady for 17th consecutive month
item.description: China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 17th straight month in October on Tuesday, in line with market expectations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for the 17th straight month in October on Tuesday, in line with market expectations. WHY IT'S IMPORTANT The steady loan prime rates (LPRs) suggest policymakers are in no rush to roll out fresh monetary easing after a strong third-quarter GDP outcome, as they focus on reforming the loan pricing framework and improving monetary policy transmission. BY THE NUMBERS The one-year loan prime rate (LPR) was kept at 3.00%, and the five-year LPR was unchanged at 3.50%. In a Reuters [USN:L1N46506U TEXT:"survey"] of 22 market participants conducted on Monday, all participants predicted no change to either of the two rates. CONTEXT China's central bank is [USN:P8N42J00P TEXT:"considering switching"] its main policy rate to the overnight reverse repurchase rate, in a shift aimed at improving the transmission of monetary policy to support the economy. The People's Bank of China will also issue policy guidance to advance reform of the loan pricing benchmark, shifting lending away from a relatively narrow reliance on the LPR toward a more diversified set of benchmarks, the bank's governor Pan Gongsheng said on Monday. Some financially strong companies could opt for either the overnight reverse repo rate or the LPR as the benchmark for floating-rate loans, while the overnight rate could also serve as an alternative pricing benchmark for bonds and financial derivatives, Pan said. China's economy [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"expanded"] 4.5% year-on-year in the third quarter, topping forecasts and reducing the urgency for Beijing to step up support to meet its annual growth target. KEY QUOTES ** Huatai Securities "The latest announcement extends the shift in the policy rate anchor toward asset-side pricing, maintaining a gradual approach. The tiered design - giving large firms the option while keeping small and micro enterprises and individuals anchored to the LPR - is primarily aimed at avoiding a one-off shock to the existing pricing system." "As more corporate loans are linked to the overnight repo rate , the rate's fluctuation range is likely to narrow, enhancing the stability of liquidity conditions."

item.title: Super-sub Boland delivers for Australia again
item.description: A test career of cameo appearances and fleeting glories has been Scott Boland's lot since his explosive Ashes debut five years ago but the pace warrior has rarely let Australia down when given half a chance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A test career of cameo appearances and fleeting glories has been Scott Boland's lot since his explosive Ashes debut five years ago but the pace warrior has rarely let Australia down when given half a chance. In Gqeberha, Boland has delivered again in his first test since January to give Australia the upper hand as they look to seal their three-match series against South Africa with a game to spare. The burly Victorian finished Monday's rain-hit day two with figures of 4-31 at St George's Park, leaving the hosts [USN:L6N46511W TEXT:"in trouble at 97 for 5"]. It takes a special bowler to deny world-class spinner Nathan Lyon a place in Australia's attack, no matter the surface or conditions. It takes an extraordinary one to operate at the highest level at the age of 37 and to hit the mark with such efficiency after a long period on the fringes. Boland knew of his selection in Australia's starting side only minutes before the toss but wasted no time finding his line and length. "Sometimes I'll take 30 balls just jumping through my action," he told reporters. "I did it the other day and it took six. I was feeling good." Boland struck in consecutive balls to remove Aiden Markram and David Bedingham on day one, then returned on day two to dismiss Marques Ackerman with his seventh ball of the afternoon. Matt Renshaw took a screamer of a slips catch to help Boland capture his fourth wicket with an edge off Ryan Rickelton's bat. Boland's haul so far in his 20th test has lowered his career bowling average to a tick over 18 -- the best of any bowler with 50 wickets since World War Two. He is Australia's oldest specialist test quick since Ray Lindwall in 1960. Heaven knows what Boland might have achieved with more opportunity in a lesser Australian attack -- or had he been plucked from Sheffield Shield obscurity well before his fairytale 2021 debut against England, when he took 6-7 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Boland said he was in no mood to slow down and would gladly play every test if selected. "I know I'm 37 and the oldest fast bowler to play for a while," he said. "But still feel like I'm going really well and my body's in good spot. I feel like I can do it for as long as I can."

item.title: Malaysia has made no commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, ministry says
item.description: Malaysia has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial assistance to budget airline operator AirAsia, the finance ministry said, though it acknowledged concerns over the carrier's financial health following a jump in jet fuel prices.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Malaysia has made no agreement or commitment to provide financial assistance to budget airline operator AirAsia, the finance ministry said, though it acknowledged concerns over the carrier's financial health following a jump in jet fuel prices. Reuters [USN:L1N45Y02T TEXT:"reported"] this month, citing sources, that AirAsia was in talks with the government over potential support. The airline's co-founder Tony Fernandes said the talks focused on aviation-related costs such as airport charges and fuel, not financial assistance In a written parliamentary reply on Monday, the finance ministry said it was monitoring developments in Malaysia's aviation sector, including recent quarterly losses reported by AirAsia that were attributed to rising fuel costs stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran The government was regularly engaging with aviation players and seeking views from industry and technical experts, as was the case for other economic sectors affected by the Middle East crisis, it said Any request for support from companies in any sector "will be considered based on the interests of the country and the people, the fiscal sustainability of the government and the protection of public funds, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures," the ministry said "To date, the government has not made any agreement or commitment to provide financing support to AirAsia, whether in the form of guarantees, loans or public fund injections," it said The ministry said AirAsia was a significant player in the aviation sector, accounting for around 41% of the 104.5 million passenger movements recorded at airports operated by Malaysia Airports Holdings in 2025 and almost 60% of domestic passenger movements The carrier also played a significant role in maintaining air connectivity in Malaysia's Sabah and Sarawak states on Borneo island, it said

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese electronics components maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing (002384.SZ) , is seeking to raise up to HK$10.67 billion ($1.36 billion) in a Hong Kong listing, according to a regulatory filing lodged on Tuesday. The Shenzhen-listed manufacturer of electronic circuit products is offering 113.8 million H shares at up to HK$93.80 each, joining a wave of mainland firms tapping a [USN:L8N463029 TEXT:"resurgent"] initial public offering market in the financial hub. Suzhou Dongshan Precision said proceeds from the offering would be used to build new and upgrade existing production facilities, including expanding high-speed EML chip and optical module manufacturing capacity in mainland China. Final pricing is scheduled for October 26, with trading of the shares expected to begin on October 28. Founded in 1998, Suzhou Dongshan Precision is the world's second-largest supplier of flexible printed circuit boards used in smartphones, automobiles and other electronic devices, according to the company's website . In Hong Kong, companies raised HK$388 billion through 118 listings in the first nine months of 2026, more than double from a year earlier, helped by strong investor appetite for Chinese technology-related stocks. item.title: Dollar and euro drift, yen slips as markets seek direction
item.description: The US dollar churned at the start of trading in Asia on Tuesday as a tepid recovery in investor confidence bolstered higher-yielding currencies, but growing political risk in Europe continued to test traders' nerves.
item.dc:creator: Gregor Hunter
item.content:encoded: The US dollar churned at the start of trading in Asia on Tuesday as a tepid recovery in investor confidence bolstered higher-yielding currencies, but growing political risk in Europe continued to test traders' nerves. The euro was steady at $1.1216, while the British pound rose 0.1% to $1.3308. The Australian dollar was up 0.1% at $0.6986, while its New Zealand counterpart nudged 0.1% higher to $0.5668. Against the yen , the US dollar was flat at 158.56 yen ahead of an auction of 20-year Japanese government bonds. "FX markets reflected the improvement in risk appetite, with higher-carry currencies finding buyers," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group in Melbourne. "Europe was less convincing," Weston said. "French sovereign risk is clearly being priced into European equities, but the euro's resilience suggests traders aren't yet treating it as a systemic European problem." French authorities set [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"curfews"] in several cities on Monday after nationwide anti-government protests plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office into [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"turmoil"]. In Italy, the government said it will [USN:L1N4650LE TEXT:"dispatch 500 troops"] after two days of unrest. "The spread of French government bonds over Germany has come under renewed widening pressure against the backdrop of violent protests grabbing the headlines," ING analysts wrote in a client note. "Tuesday will likely see more headlines around the 2027 budget, as (the French) Parliament is slated for a first formal vote on the revenue section of the finance bill." The spread between French and German 10-year government bonds widened 9.9 basis points on Monday to 147.3 basis points. The yield on the US 10-year Treasury bond was flat at 5.131%. The US dollar index , which measures the greenback's strength against six currencies, ended two days of loss on Monday, rising 0.2% to 101.98. Against the Chinese yuan , the dollar was flat at 6.6811 yuan in offshore trade after the People's Bank of China kept interest rates on hold, in line with market expectations. Bitcoin was flat at $81,906.58, while ether nudged 0.3% higher to $2,405.99.

item.title: Brent crude holds near five-month high on Middle East tension
item.description: Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
item.dc:creator: Anjana Anil, Siyi Liu
item.content:encoded: Oil prices advanced on Tuesday, with Brent hovering around a five-month high as traders priced in a geopolitical risk premium from Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Brent crude futures climbed 55 cents, or 0.50%, to $110.10 a barrel by 0319 GMT, after rising as high as $110.70 a barrel in the previous session to their highest since May 20. The US West Texas Intermediate crude (WTI) contract for November delivery , set to expire on Tuesday, was up 0.24% to $103.91. The more-active December contract rose 39 cents, or 0.40%, to $98.93. "Oil prices remain well-supported ... This suggests the market is pricing in a significant risk premium, given the situation's volatility," ING analysts said in a note on Tuesday. "However, if flows continue uninhibited despite the geopolitical environment, the risk premium would likely erode slowly. Clearly, there are no signs of this yet." At least 18 vessels were reportedly attacked over two weeks, which keeps the risk premium intact, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday. HOUTHIS CLAIM ATTACKS ON SAUDI FACILITIES Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they launched [USN:S8N44M08Y TEXT:"several attacks"] on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco (2222.SE) site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Abha airport. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims and Reuters could not independently verify them. Also on Monday, a Houthi [USN:L1N46509O TEXT:"attack"] on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 58 people with more than 200 injured. The renewed attacks heightened fears about regional stability and underscored continuing risks to energy supply from the region, keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel. In the US, crude oil stockpiles were expected to have fallen last week along with product inventories, a preliminary Reuters [USN:L4N4651EI TEXT:"poll"] showed on Monday. Friday's [USN:L1N463009 TEXT:"executive order"] by President Donald Trump waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including goods duties and penalties for purchases of its energy. However, Trump said on Saturday he had yet to announce a [USN:L6N464042 TEXT:"final decision"] on the matter, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials wanted more time to evaluate the situation. Russia's crude [USN:L1N46008R TEXT:"oil production"] increased by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million bpd, but remained about 870,000 bpd below that of a year ago, the International Energy Agency said last week. "While the prospect of additional Russian diesel supply offers some theoretical relief, traders appear far more focused on the ongoing risk of further damage to energy infrastructure across the Gulf region," said Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst.

item.title: Cuba accuses US of letting terrorists operate with impunity after speedboat raid
item.description: Cuban law enforcement officials on Monday alleged that the US was allowing terrorists to operate with impunity on American soil, citing details of an investigation into a February speedboat incursion that led to a gun battle at sea, deaths and injuries on both sides.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cuban law enforcement officials on Monday alleged that the US was allowing terrorists to operate with impunity on American soil, citing details of an investigation into a February speedboat incursion that led to a gun battle at sea, deaths and injuries on both sides. On February 25, 10 Cuban exiles attempted to infiltrate the island nation by boat from the Florida Keys, armed with nearly 13,000 rounds of ammunition, 11 rifles, 15 handguns, Molotov cocktails, a VHF radio and Starlink satellite communication equipment, according to the Cuban investigation that was described by state-run media on Monday. Five were killed; the rest, including some who were wounded, are in custody and face terrorism charges, authorities said. Cuba said on Monday that its investigation, which included confessions from those detained by its authorities, found that some of those involved in training insurgents remain at large in the US. "It is also important to highlight ... the crimes still being committed today by individuals and organizations that, from within the United States, provided the property used to carry out these acts, arranged and secured land and maritime transport, and facilitated the purchase and stockpiling of weaponry," said Cuban prosecutor Edward Roberts. Cuban authorities accused Maritza Lugo Fernandez, a Cuban national residing in Florida, of helping to organize the alleged plot. Some of those detained confessed they had trained on a farm property in Florida owned by Lugo Fernandez, who leads the Florida-based "Partido Democrático 30 de Noviembre," or the Democratic Party of November 30. Lugo Fernandez denies the allegations. "For more than 40 years, that regime has accused me of being a terrorist - of everything they can possibly come up with ... ," she said in a clip included in the state-run media report. "Personally, I live with peace of mind; I’m not concerned about what they say because I am very clear - fully aware - that it is all a lie." Neither the US Embassy in Cuba nor the US Department of Justice responded to a Reuters request for comment on the Cuban government's allegations. Cuba and the FBI previously said they were cooperating on the investigation. According to Cuban authorities, several of those detained in February said they planned simultaneous attacks on police and border guard units in Matanzas, a province just east of Havana, with the goal of inciting an armed uprising and triggering a US military intervention. The accusations come as the US has piled pressure on Cuba's government, including a nine-month de facto fuel blockade and reinforced sanctions that have led to an unprecedented economic crisis on the island. The US has called the Cuban government corrupt and says it is seeking a change in leadership there.

item.title: South Korea central bank to hold rates on October 22, hike in November
item.description: The Bank of Korea will keep its key policy rate unchanged on Thursday after two consecutive increases but is expected to raise borrowing costs once more next month, a Reuters poll of economists found, as inflation remains above target and growth remains firm.
item.dc:creator: Renusri K
item.content:encoded: The Bank of Korea will keep its key policy rate unchanged on Thursday after two consecutive increases but is expected to raise borrowing costs once more next month, a Reuters poll of economists found, as inflation remains above target and growth remains firm. Consumer inflation eased to 2.9% in [USN:L1N45N18N TEXT:"September"] from 3.1% in August, but remained above the BOK's 2% target. Strong semiconductor-led growth, a recovery in domestic demand and elevated energy costs are likely to keep underlying price pressures firm. Still, the recent moderation in headline inflation and Governor Shin Hyun Song's call for time to assess the effects of the [USN:L4N44N0CI TEXT:"back-to-back"] hikes give policymakers room to pause this month rather than deliver a third consecutive increase. All 34 economists surveyed by Reuters from October 14 to 19 expected the Bank of Korea (BOK) to hold its seven-day repurchase rate (KROCRT=ECI) at 3.00% at its October 22 meeting. "We think the BOK will buy some time, but ... that does not mean it is done with the hiking cycle," said Jeeho Yoon, senior economist at BNP Paribas. "The risks are tilted to the upside, given that growth is very strong on the back of semiconductors. This strong growth will spread into the domestic sector and domestic demand, (leading) to inflationary pressures." WEIGHING FINANCIAL STABILITY RISKS Asia's fourth-largest economy grew [USN:L1N43O1HA TEXT:"0.6%"] in the April to June quarter and 3.7% from a year earlier. The poll forecasts 3.5% growth this year, while next week's third-quarter GDP data may show whether the export-led recovery is broadening into domestic demand. Inflation is forecast to average 2.7% this year before easing to 2.2% in 2027. With growth expected to remain firm and inflation above target, median forecasts in the survey showed the BOK raising its base rate to 3.25% at its November meeting, in line with the BOK's dot plot projection. The rate is then forecast to rise to 3.50% in the first quarter of 2027 and stay there for the rest of the year. This is 25 basis points above the forecast in the previous poll, conducted before the August decision. "The November hike is still likely because the BOK's CPI projections show inflation is expected to stay at about 2% for most of 2027," said Michelle Lam, an economist at Societe Generale, who expects two more rate hikes after October in her baseline scenario. "Also, if you look at the housing market, house prices are still rising. Even though household mortgage borrowing is slowing, it does not seem that rate hikes have done enough to slow the housing market. So there is still room for the BOK to hike." Beyond inflation and growth, the BOK is also weighing financial-stability risks, particularly developments in housing, household debt and financial markets. The benchmark KOSPI index (.KS11) hit a [USN:L1N46101G TEXT:"six-month low"] on Thursday and triggered a circuit breaker for the 10th time this year, underscoring heightened market volatility. "In terms of the household (wealth) effect, of course it will affect confidence but 50% of household assets are in housing and equities account for only 10%. The impact of an equity-market correction would not be as much as that of a correction in house prices," Lam added. "If the equity-market correction continues, I think that may also affect the BOK's pace of monetary policy tightening." ([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from Reuters global economic poll)

item.title: Asesinato de exfiscal anticorrupción es un sombrío hito en violencia política en Guatemala
item.description: El asesinato el fin de semana del abogado anticorrupción Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, quien se hizo de poderosos enemigos al enfrentarse a la élite guatemalteca, constituye uno de los homicidios políticos más significativos del país en las últimas décadas, lo que reaviva la preocupación por la vulnerabilidad de quienes luchan contra la corrupción en Centroamérica.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu, Raul Cortes
item.content:encoded: El asesinato el fin de semana del abogado anticorrupción Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, quien se hizo de poderosos enemigos al enfrentarse a la élite guatemalteca, constituye uno de los homicidios políticos más significativos del país en las últimas décadas, lo que reaviva la preocupación por la vulnerabilidad de quienes luchan contra la corrupción en Centroamérica. Familiares, amigos y simpatizantes velaron el lunes a Solórzano, de 43 años, dos días después de que sus agresores lo asesinaran a tiros en un centro deportivo de la Ciudad de Guatemala. Su sepelio está programado para el martes. La policía guatemalteca informó haber detenido a dos hombres vinculados al homicidio y dijo haber incautado un rifle tipo carabina y una motocicleta. Ambos fueron puestos en libertad el domingo sin cargos y mantienen su inocencia. La policía indicó que aún no ha determinado el móvil del crimen. Para los guatemaltecos, el crimen trajo a la memoria el sombrío asesinato en 1998 del obispo Juan José Gerardi, quien fue golpeado hasta la muerte dos días después de presentar un informe que documentaba las atrocidades de la guerra civil de la nación centroamericana, culpando al Ejército y a sus fuerzas aliadas de la mayor parte de la violencia. "Esa magnitud y relevancia (no habíamos visto) yo creo que desde 1998 que asesinaron al padre Gerardi", dijo Juan Francisco Sandoval, exjefe de la Fiscalía Especial contra la Impunidad de Guatemala. SOLÓRZANO SEÑALÓ A LA ÉLITE Solórzano Foppa era hijo de un combatiente que murió en la guerra civil en la década de 1980 y nieto de la aclamada poeta y activista Alaíde Foppa, quien fue secuestrada en 1980 y de la que nunca más se supo. El abogado pasó de fiscal adjunto a convertirse en una figura destacada en la lucha contra la corrupción. Trabajó con la CICIG, el grupo anticorrupción respaldado por la ONU, en el caso de soborno "La Línea", que provocó la caída del presidente Otto Pérez Molina en 2015. Como director de la agencia tributaria de Guatemala desde 2016, se centró en la élite empresarial. Obtuvo un acuerdo récord de 100 millones de dólares con la siderúrgica Aceros de Guatemala e hizo arrestar al dueño del hotel Camino Real por falsificación de facturas. Sus casos permitieron recuperar aproximadamente 280 millones de dólares en impuestos. "Él tenía muchos adversarios por su trabajo en la autoridad tributaria, tenía muchos adversarios de naturaleza política, sobre todo a partir de las denuncias públicas que él realizó", dijo Sandoval, quien conocía a Solórzano Foppa desde hacía 23 años. El exfiscal fue destituido en 2018 y la CICIG se vio obligada a dimitir como parte de una reacción violenta de la poderosa élite guatemalteca. En 2021, fue arrestado bajo acusaciones de irregularidades en la recolección de firmas para registrar un nuevo partido político. "Esto no me avergüenza, avergüenza a los que están robando", dijo Solórzano Foppa en aquel momento, mostrando las esposas en sus muñecas a los periodistas en el tribunal. "Esto demuestra que estamos afectando a las personas poderosas de este país", añadió. Posteriormente, un juez desestimó los cargos más graves. En 2023, se unió brevemente al equipo de defensa del periodista de investigación del país centroamericano José Rubén Zamora, arrestado por cargos de lavado de dinero pero que afirmó ser un preso político. Solórzano solía decir que existían vínculos entre bandas criminales y partidos políticos, así como con el sistema judicial. "Me duele mucho porque no era la forma de cómo cortarle la vida a un ciudadano que le ha servido tanto al país", dijo el exministro de Gobernación Francisco Rivas, amigo de Solórzano Foppa durante 20 años. "Era una persona muy luchadora, extraordinariamente valiente, muy fuerte en cuanto a sus convicciones y valores". El presidente Bernardo Arévalo, quien hizo campaña como defensor de la lucha contra la corrupción en las elecciones que ganó en 2023, también condenó el asesinato, calificándolo el sábado como un hecho "cobarde". "Sus autores, materiales e intelectuales deben pagar las consecuencias con todo el peso de la ley”, afirmó. Solórzano Foppa deja cuatro hijos: dos de su primer matrimonio y dos con una segunda pareja. El tío del abogado, el activista de derechos humanos Julio Solórzano, sugirió que el asesinato podría ser una forma de generar miedo y desconfianza y desestabilizar el país. "Esperamos que pronto se sepa quiénes fueron los autores, pero el impacto como un crimen político ahí está", dijo durante el velatorio del lunes.

item.title: South Korea's Elice plunges 30% in market debut as data centre stocks shunned
item.description: Shares in South Korean AI services firm Elice Group plummeted 30% in their market debut on Tuesday, amid a sharp retreat in sentiment towards the sector that has also derailed other planned listings.
item.dc:creator: Heejin Kim, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: Shares in South Korean AI services firm Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) plummeted 30% in their market debut on Tuesday, amid a sharp retreat in sentiment towards the sector that has also derailed other planned listings. Elice, which raised 201.1 billion won ($150 million) in its IPO, provides AI cloud services as well as AI-based education and business software and plans to spend most of its IPO proceeds on launching portable modular data centres and related infrastructure. Investors are increasingly questioning whether massive AI spending can pay off anytime soon as elevated inflation keeps borrowing costs high. Analysts noted that Elice's IPO had been priced on October 6, before the recent selloff in AI-related stocks. "Elice's debut shows the AI infrastructure trade has moved from 'build at any cost' to 'who is paying and for how long'," said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based Shenton Research. "Until the AI labs that rent ... capacity show they can fund their compute commitments, new listings across the region will likely be priced in that risk premium." This month, data centre firms that have shelved their IPO plans include Australia's [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"Firmus"], which is backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Blackstone (BX.N) -backed [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"AirTrunk"], which postponed a Singapore REIT IPO, as well as [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"SB Energy"], a unit of Japanese tech investment conglomerate SoftBank (9984.T) , which had filed paperwork for a US IPO. "Everyone is not sure how much demand for AI there will be and it is hard to estimate current demand," added Kim Hak-joon, an analyst at Seoul-based Kiwoom Securities. Elice's shares were last trading at 63,600 won compared with its IPO pricing of 90,500 won. The IPO drew institutional orders worth 388.84 times the shares available in the offering, according to a filing. The company has said revenue for the first half of the year tripled to 34 billion won and that it swung to an operating profit of 10 billion won compared with a 3.5 billion won loss for the same period a year earlier.

item.title: Lula nega que tenha armado bomba fiscal com medidas recentes
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, negou nesta segunda-feira que medidas adotadas por seu governo nos últimos dias como o reajuste do Bolsa Família e o perdão de dívidas de microempreendedores individuais (MEI) sejam uma bomba fiscal e afirmou que há espaço no orçamento para todas elas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, negou nesta segunda-feira que medidas adotadas por seu governo nos últimos dias como o reajuste do Bolsa Família e o perdão de dívidas de microempreendedores individuais (MEI) sejam uma bomba fiscal e afirmou que há espaço no orçamento para todas elas. "Eu não sei de onde você tirou essa ideia de que é uma bomba que vai estourar...Não é bomba", disse o presidente a uma das jornalistas que o entrevistava. "Tudo o que está sendo aprovado está nas possibilidades fiscais e no orçamento", afirmou. Especialistas do mercado financeiro avaliam as medidas como eleitoreiras e consideram que devem impactar negativamente as contas públicas. "Eu não preciso aprender responsabilidade com a Faria Lima. Responsabilidade eu tenho, porque eu sei como pai de família, como trabalhador de fábrica que recebe salário, que a gente não pode gastar o que a gente não tem e portanto nós estamos gastando aquilo que nós sabemos que é possível fazer e vamos fazer", disse Lula, na entrevista. Mais cedo nesta segunda-feira, Ministério do Planejamento e Orçamento informou em nota à imprensa que deve remanejar cerca de R$20 bilhões das contas federais de 2027 para acomodar medidas adotadas recentemente, destacando que o valor corresponde a pouco mais de 1% do total de despesas sujeitas ao limite de gastos. Sem detalhar a quais ações esse impacto se refere, a pasta disse na nota que os ajustes serão propostos ao Congresso Nacional mantendo o limite total das despesas e a meta de resultado primário.

item.title: Report: Multiple teams in mix to acquire Jets G Connor Hellebuyck
item.description: At least three teams remain involved in trade discussions for Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck as the end of his team-issued suspension approaches, ESPN reported Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least three teams remain involved in trade discussions for Winnipeg Jets goaltender Connor Hellebuyck as the end of his team-issued suspension approaches, ESPN reported Monday. A deal is not guaranteed before Hellebuyck's suspension expires Friday, according to the report. If Winnipeg still has not moved him, the Jets are expected to begin paying the three-time Vezina Trophy winner while continuing to keep him away from the team. Hellebuyck, 33, has been suspended without pay since failing to report for training camp after requesting a trade during the offseason. Sportsnet reported Saturday that Hellebuyck informed Winnipeg before its Oct. 2 season opener that he intended to return. The Jets then exercised their authority to impose a disciplinary suspension scheduled to expire Oct. 23. The NHL's collective bargaining agreement permits a disciplinary suspension of a "reasonable length" for a player who returns after missing training camp without permission. Hellebuyck has forfeited nearly $39,000 per day in salary, bringing his estimated losses to nearly $800,000 through Monday, according to ESPN. He has continued skating regularly in Michigan. The former Hart Trophy winner asked Winnipeg to move him this summer after spending his entire NHL career with the franchise. Hellebuyck has a full no-movement clause, giving him control over any potential destination. He is in the third season of a seven-year, $59.5 million contract. His no-movement protection changes to a modified no-trade clause next summer. Hellebuyck won his third Vezina Trophy in 2025 and also captured the Hart Trophy as the NHL's most valuable player that season. He helped the United States win Olympic gold in February. Winnipeg has opened the season 4-2-2 without Hellebuyck, with Stuart Skinner and Clay Stevenson handling the goaltending duties while general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff continues exploring trade options. --Field Level Media

item.title: OpenAI seeks to accelerate fundraising ahead of Anthropic IPO, sources say
item.description: The ChatGPT maker is racing to secure investor commitments in an unusually fast fundraising that could value the company at over $1.4 trillion, according to two people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wang, Krystal Hu, Sabrina Valle
item.content:encoded: OpenAI is racing to secure investor commitments before rival [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"Anthropic's expected public market debut"] in mid-November, in an unusually fast fundraising that could value the ChatGPT maker at over $1.4 trillion, according to two people familiar with the matter. The rapid timetable reflects, in part, a desire to get ahead of Anthropic as the two frontier labs are increasingly tapping in to a similar investor base, the people said, adding that OpenAI wants to capitalize on its recent revenue growth after launching new models. SoftBank Group (9984.T) , Abu Dhabi-based MGX and other existing backers of OpenAI are in talks to join the round of about $30 billion, one of the people said. The acceleration underscores how closely the two AI developers are competing for capital as both pursue trillion-dollar price tags, amid growing concern about rising interest rates, significant volatility in technology stocks and rising scrutiny of AI valuations. OpenAI held meetings with long-only funds and sovereign wealth funds last week while Anthropic was hosting its own [USN:L6N4601AA TEXT:"investor day"]. OpenAI's funding round is expected to move faster than is typical for an offering of its size, the people said. Investors familiar with the company say OpenAI also needs capital to fund its substantial infrastructure commitments and bolster its balance sheet if a deterioration in the IPO markets further delays its planned 2027 listing. Though there is high demand for the shares of both companies, investors face the challenge of evaluating and allocating capital to two complex, competing offerings within days or weeks of each other. Some investors view OpenAI’s financing push as an effort to lock in capital from funds that might otherwise devote more of their resources to Anthropic’s IPO, the people said. OpenAI and SoftBank declined to comment. Anthropic and MGX did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TRYING TO HEAD OFF COMPARISONS OpenAI is pitching investors on growth that accelerated after the launch of its GPT-6 Astra model, saying it had reached $50 billion in annualized revenue and expecting that figure to rise to $70 billion by year-end, according to one of the people. OpenAI has also cut prices on its cheaper models, which it said has boosted usage, and told investors it can further lower the price of AI models, the person added. Anthropic's annualized revenue reached roughly $65 billion by July, Reuters previously reported. Its quarterly revenue jumped to $16.8 billion in the third quarter from $11.6 billion in the second quarter this year, it told investors, but slowing month-to-month revenue growth has raised concerns among investors about [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"its valuation"]. OpenAI is seeking to complete the fundraising before Anthropic’s financial disclosures give investors a fuller picture of its business and invite comparisons between the two companies, one person said. The disclosures could prompt investors to press OpenAI Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar for more details about the company’s revenue growth and financial outlook, the person added. OpenAI records revenue on a net basis by subtracting partner shares upfront. It has [USN:L6N42D13P TEXT:"accused Anthropic of inflating"] its revenue by counting the full, gross value of contracts sold through third-party cloud providers. Anthropic told Reuters earlier that it follows established accounting practices. "OpenAI could want to set its own valuation and not have to worry about a comp (comparison)," said Edward Best, co-chair of capital markets at Willkie Farr & Gallagher, who is not working on the deal and commented on a hypothetical basis. "It's really a two-horse race in terms of being public." [USN:L6N40K172 TEXT:"OpenAI was last valued at $852 billion"] in March this year, after a record-breaking $122 billion funding round, including a commitment from Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , which agreed to invest up to $50 billion in the lab. The Financial Times previously reported some details of OpenAI’s potential fundraising. IPO PLANS HIT BY MARKET JITTERS A number of companies preparing to go public have decided to wait until after Anthropic’s planned IPO, wary of competing for investor demand amid market volatility and a pullback in AI stocks, bankers and investors said. Some late-stage companies are also timing private fundraising rounds to avoid coinciding with Anthropic’s expected debut, the bankers and investors said. Some existing and prospective Anthropic investors have argued for a valuation closer to [USN:L6N46118I TEXT:"$1.5 trillion"] for its market debut — instead of the desired $2 trillion — after the AI startup's third-quarter results fell short of expectations, Reuters reported last week. The reassessment comes amid a choppy market since September, with volatility in oil prices, rising bond yields and growing concerns about AI safety weighing on investor appetite for technology stocks. Investors are also scrutinizing the cost of AI infrastructure, including the debt needed to finance the data centers powering the boom. At the center of the latest concerns is cloud provider CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"whose shares and debt tumbled last week"] as investors scrutinized the nearly $50 billion in borrowings used to fund its rapid expansion. The uncertainty has disrupted what had been expected to be a busy autumn for IPOs, with companies reassessing their listing plans amid market volatility and concerns about valuations. Blackstone (BX.N) -backed AirTrunk REIT, Nvidia (NVDA.O) -backed Firmus and SoftBank-backed SB Energy have either [USN:L4N45Z0RI TEXT:"pulled or paused their listings"]. Nuclear services company Holtec cited a "perfect storm," driven mainly by uncertainty around data-center demand, when it [USN:L4N45H14U TEXT:"pulled its US listing last month"]. Companies in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, widely viewed as a proxy for AI-related semiconductor demand, have shed $1.6 trillion in less than two weeks, while AI infrastructure companies have come under particular pressure.

item.title: Hegseth meets Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, Axios reports
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, Axios reported, citing two sources with knowledge.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, Axios reported, citing two sources with knowledge. Reuters could not immediately confirm the meeting, but Hegseth said in a social media post that he had visited US service members in the Central Command area of responsibility, which covers the Middle East, northeast Africa and parts of Asia. The Pentagon declined comment, while Israel's embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. News of Hegseth's trip comes a day after US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N46403J TEXT:"endorsed"] Netanyahu in next week's parliamentary election in Israel - its first vote since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023, that shook the country and plunged the Middle East into turmoil, as Israel went to war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu's religious-nationalist coalition is projected to lose its governing majority, although the opposition may also struggle to form a government, opinion polls show. US Vice President JD Vance, however, declined to endorse Netanyahu in an interview earlier on Monday, saying he was not getting involved in Israeli elections. "I endorse American candidates, and that's where I'm focused on is the midterms," Vance, who traveled to Budapest and [USN:L1N40Q06M TEXT:"endorsed"] Viktor Orban in Hungarian election earlier this year, said in an interview with digital media outlet 2WAY. "I'm not anti-endorsing him, but I'm not pro-endorsing him, I'm not getting involved in Israeli elections." Vance said.

item.title: US says travelers should reconsider Kenya trips on health risks amid Ebola spread
item.description: The US State Department said on Monday it has asked Americans to reconsider any travel to Kenya and raised its travel advisory for the African nation due to health risks.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: The US State Department said on Monday it has asked Americans to reconsider any travel to Kenya and raised its travel advisory for the African nation due to health risks. "The level was changed from Level 2 to Level 3 due to health risks," the travel advisory by the US embassy in Kenya said. The advisory was raised to level 3, which asks Americans to reconsider travel, from an earlier level 2 that urges increased caution. "Reconsider travel to Kenya due to risk of health, crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest, and traffic safety. Some areas have increased risk," the advisory read. Kenya confirmed [USN:L8N4640AV TEXT:"one more Ebola case"] on Sunday, bringing the total number of infections in the country to eight. Kenya has been on heightened alert, as a major Ebola outbreak centered in Congo [USN:L1N46401K TEXT:"has spread"] across borders in the region. Congo confirmed on Sunday that its outbreak had spread to an eighth province, North Ubangi, underscoring concerns about wider regional transmission. "Medical services in Kenya are limited. They are often unavailable in rural areas. Medical facilities in Kenya often lack sufficient medicine and equipment," the US travel advisory on Kenya said in its summary.

item.title: Australian lawmaker loses leg after vehicle attack being probed by anti-terror police
item.description: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose
item.content:encoded: Doctors have amputated the leg of an Australian lawmaker after a man rammed her with his car and then reversed to hit her a second time, local media and officials said on Tuesday, in an incident being investigated by anti-terrorism police. Helen Haines, an independent, underwent surgery overnight and remained in critical condition after Monday's attack in the small rural town of Wangaratta, north of Melbourne. The motive for the attack has yet to be revealed, but Australia’s prime minister has linked it to a climate of ugly, polarised political debate in the country. "It's clear that there was a deliberate act here. This wasn't an accident, someone just skidding off the road," Albanese told ABC News. Early investigations suggested the car hit Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, he said. Australian media, citing unidentified sources, reported Haines had lost one leg as a result of her injuries and that doctors were working to save the other leg. A 43-year-old man was arrested following the attack, with counter-terrorism authorities among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. Police are considering potential charges, including causing harm to a public official - an offence that carries a maximum penalty of 10 years' imprisonment - as they work to establish a motive for the attack. "At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident," Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said. STRUCK TWO TIMES Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told ABC Radio that witnesses said the alleged attacker reversed the vehicle and struck Haines a second time before a bystander intervened. Ricky Jefferies ran from his barber shop, restraining the attacker and removing a knife from him after initially believing the incident was a car accident, Australian media reported. "I heard a loud bang with no brakes. It was crazy, I just ran out to the front to see what's happening," Jefferies told reporters outside his shop. "I didn't realise the seriousness of the situation initially, and once it became relevant I just did what I could and what others were already trying to do." 'TURN TEMPERATURE DOWN' Violent attacks on politicians are extremely rare in Australia, where federal lawmakers, state leaders and even prime ministers are regularly seen in supermarkets and coffee shops, attending community events and chatting with voters with minimal security. [USN:L4N4650NF TEXT:"Haines"] worked in nursing and midwifery and as an academic before being elected to parliament as an independent in 2019 in the seat of Indi. She retained the seat in 2022 and 2025. Outside the hospital where Haines is being treated, Melbourne resident Shawn Hill said the attack showed that "the political climate is becoming more and more polarising today." "No one deserves to be put at risk of anything, especially someone who is serving the people and trying to do what is best for the Australian community," Hill told Reuters. Albanese urged Australians to engage more respectfully with one another, expressing concern about growing division in the country. He also noted a "significant increase" in threats against politicians in recent years. "We all have a responsibility to turn the temperature down," Albanese said. "I really don't want to see the character of Australia change."

item.title: UniCredit to buy back securities-services unit from Societe Generale, document shows
item.description: Italy's second-biggest bank, UniCredit , has signed an agreement to repurchase its securities-services business from French peer Societe Generale , according to a union document seen by Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's second-biggest bank, UniCredit (CRDI.MI) , has signed an agreement to repurchase its securities-services business from French peer Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) , according to a union document seen by Reuters on Monday. The unit, which looks after investors' securities and handles related administrative services, has 54 staff in Milan and Turin, according to the document, which did not provide any financial details of the agreement. Societe Generale bought UniCredit's securities services unit in 2006, striking a long-term partnership to handle those services for the Italian bank. The supply contract was last renewed in 2017 until 2026. UniCredit is seeking to bring in-house activities it deems strategic, and the transaction is part of that effort, the document said. Handling the securities itself will reduce the need for an external supplier and improve use of the business' data, UniCredit and Societe Generale did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: National Australia Bank to cut 2,500 jobs in cost overhaul as credit growth slows
item.description: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it will shed up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in the next year to simplify its operations and cut costs while the nation's credit growth remains under pressure.
item.dc:creator: Scott Murdoch, Rajasik Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB.AX) said on Tuesday it will shed up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in the next year to simplify its operations and cut costs while the nation's credit growth remains under pressure. The bank, which is Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender, said up to 1,500 roles would go by the end of 2026. The biggest cuts will target corporate roles rather than customer-facing bankers, it said. It also plans to materially reduce its use of consultants and contractors. "Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank," Chief Executive Andrew Irvine said in a statement. NAB stock was down nearly 2.5% on Tuesday, and recorded the largest share price decline of Australia's "Big Four" retail banks in the session. The S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) was down 0.9%. NAB said it would begin consultation with the Finance Sector Union, whose national assistant secretary Nicole McPherson said the job cuts would not help simplify the organisation. "To take a wrecking ball to 6% of one of Australia's largest workforces this close to Christmas is disgraceful and shows that NAB's leadership is completely detached from the lived experience of their workers," she said. The overhaul will result in a restructuring charge of about A$300 million ($209 million) before tax in 2027, related to redundancy, redeployment and organisational redesign costs. The charge compares with about A$80 million before tax incurred in each of 2025 and 2026, NAB said. The job cuts follow a period of mounting pressure on Australia's banks as weaker housing activity, rising competition and higher operating costs weigh on earnings. [USN:L1N44D060 TEXT:"In August"], NAB warned that housing credit growth would slow sharply in 2027 following the [USN:L4N42409E TEXT:"federal government's property tax"] reforms, which the bank said had dampened demand from homebuyers and investors. At that time, Irvine said the combined effects of geopolitical uncertainty, higher domestic interest rates and tax changes were creating challenges for customers. NAB employed 41,880 people globally as of September 30, 2025, according to its latest annual report. The move follows a similar restructuring drive at rival ANZ (ANZ.AX) , which last year announced plans to cut about [USN:L3N3UV1F1 TEXT:"3,500 jobs"] by September 2026 as part of a simplification program under CEO Nuno Matos to reduce duplication and lower costs. ($1 = 1.4329 Australian dollars)

item.content:encoded:
[USN:L6N4650KA TEXT:"Wall Street"] recovered some ground on Monday as investors bought back beaten-down [USN:L4N4650VO TEXT:"tech stocks"] and looked forward to key earnings reports, while easing worries over AI also cooled last week's safe-haven demand for bonds and pushed yields higher. Unrest and riots in [USN:L1N4650EF TEXT:"France"], meanwhile, weighed heavily on French bond prices and pushed the euro lower. In [USN:L6N4620ZO TEXT:"my column today"], I look at AI's pivotal role in exacerbating global imbalances and driving global capital flows. The two are increasingly connected. US yields up around 3-4 bps across the curve. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N464059 TEXT:"Oil"] mixed — Brent -0.5%, WTI +2%.

Today's Talking Points: Political risk sizzles [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"France"], [USN:S8N442025 TEXT:"Brazil"], [USN:L1N4600TJ TEXT:"the US "]— just a few of the countries where polarized politics and looming elections are becoming increasingly important risk factors for investors to consider. France isn't the only country in Europe — or the world — facing unenviable fiscal challenges, but the riots spreading across the country are unlikely to make meeting them any easier. Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday in a closely contested runoff presidential election vote, and the US midterm elections barely two weeks away could see President Donald Trump's Republican Party lose control of both houses of Congress. Affordability, inflation, high energy prices, and worries over job security amid the AI revolution are issues dominating the national conversation in every country. Policymakers gathered in Bangkok for the IMF/World Bank meetings last week shared calls for fiscal discipline, AI vigilance, and tackling global trade imbalances. But that's easier said than done when domestic politics are so fractured everywhere, and the spirit of multilateralism is its lowest in decades. FXing a hole China's economy grew by 4.5% in the third quarter, official figures on Monday showed. The good news — that was faster than economists had expected; the not so good news — it was driven by roaring exports, which are putting the country on course to top last year's record $1.2 trillion trade surplus. China's bulging surplus is a key contributor to the expanding global imbalances that the IMF and others are warning about. Perhaps the rising yuan will help wean the economy off exports and support domestic demand. The yuan has been appreciating steadily for the last 18 months, and is now at a 4-year high against the dollar. But the yuan's broader 'real effective exchange rate,' or REER, is still on the weak side. Yes, its REER value has risen 7% since May last year, but it's also around 15% weaker than it was four years ago and right now is right on its average of the past 20 years. AI boomerang After last week's selloff, the global AI trade got off to a stronger start this week. At least, with tech earnings about to begin rolling out, sentiment in the US improved — the 'SOX' semiconductor index on Monday snapped an eight-day losing streak, its worst run since October 2008. The 2.5% rise on Monday is a good start, but there's more to go if last week's 11.5% slump is to be clawed back. Similarly, South Korea's KOSPI's 4% rebound in the last two trading sessions will be welcomed, but the index is still down around 20% from where it was two weeks ago. Like politics mentioned above, AI sentiment is becoming increasingly polarized. Few people doubt the technology's transformative significance, but bulls and bears are digging in for the long haul. All eyes are now on US earnings, and whether the incoming numbers and company outlooks justify the (still) lofty stock prices. What could move markets tomorrow?
